'''Carisa Hendrix''' (born 1987) is a Canadian [[Magic (illusion)|magician]], [[comedian]], and [[fire eater]] who often performs in the persona of '''Lucy Darling''', inspired by the wisecracking socialite characters from the [[Classical Hollywood cinema|Golden Age of Hollywood.]]

==Personal life==

Hendrix was born in [[Prince Albert, Saskatchewan]], in 1987.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Livingstone |first1=Barb |title=Compelling Calgarians: Carisa Hendrix |url=https://calgaryherald.com/news/local-news/compelling-calgarians-carisa-hendrix |access-date=27 November 2025 |work=Calgary Herald |date=January 2, 2020}}</ref><ref name="allabout">{{Cite web|url=https://www.carisahendrix.com/about/|title=All About Carisa Hendrix - Carisa Hendrix <nowiki>|</nowiki> Award Winning Circus Stunt Girl & Fire Eater <nowiki>|</nowiki> Calgary & Edmonton|publisher=Carisa Hendrix|website=carisahendrix.com|accessdate=April 11, 2020}}</ref> They<ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.carisahendrix.com/about |access-date=2026-03-13 |website=Carisa Hendrix |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Creating characters with Carisa Hendrix |url=https://kingstontheatre.ca/creating-characters-with-carisa-hendrix-a-lucy-darling-story/ |website=Kingston Theatre |access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref> grew up and are based in [[Calgary]].<ref name="allabout" />

Hendrix's interest in magic began while watching a [[David Copperfield (illusionist)|David Copperfield]] special with their father at the age of six or seven.<ref name="Davis" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Magic comes home: Carisa Hendrix returns to Calgary {{!}} Watch News Videos Online |url=https://globalnews.ca/video/10236591/magic-comes-home-carisa-hendrix-returns-to-calgary/ |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=Global News |language=en-US}}</ref> Later, while volunteering at a library, they created a well-received magic trick involving library cards.<ref name="Davis">{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Andrew |date=November 28, 2023 |title=PERFORMANCE Teatro Zinzanni's Carisa Hendrix talks magic, queerness and Canada |url=https://windycitytimes.com/2023/11/28/performance-teatro-zinzannis-carisa-hendrix-talks-magic-queerness-and-canada/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208054422/https://windycitytimes.com/2023/11/28/performance-teatro-zinzannis-carisa-hendrix-talks-magic-queerness-and-canada/ |archive-date=December 8, 2025 |access-date=December 8, 2025 |website=Windy City Times}}</ref>

At the age of 16, Hendrix was kicked out of the family home. Needing to make money, they worked a variety of retail jobs, and at a haunted house for $50 per night, performing a ten minute set using skills learned from sideshow performers at a youth summer arts program, such as fire eating.<ref name="Davis" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2025-02-03 |title=Carisa Hendrix opens up about her life and career |url=https://magiciansworkshop.blog/2025/02/03/carisa-hendrix-opens-up-about-her-life-and-career/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525075411/https://magiciansworkshop.blog/2025/02/03/carisa-hendrix-opens-up-about-her-life-and-career/ |archive-date=May 25, 2025 |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=The Magician's Workshop Blog |language=en}}</ref>

Hendrix began booking gigs, learning additional skills such as [[Stilts|stilt walking]], which allowed them to leave retail jobs and focus on performing. They incorporated a comedic flair, combining magic with circus arts.<ref name=":2" />

In 2007, Hendrix was accepted at the [[Alberta University of the Arts|Alberta College of Art and Design]], studying a variety of performance skills including acting, magic, [[vaudeville]], [[burlesque]] and modeling.<ref name=":3" />

Their career skyrocketed following an invitation by an Italian world record television show to break the record for Torch Teething, which is holding a flaming torch between the teeth.<ref name=":2" />  

Hendrix identifies as [[gay]], [[non-binary]], and a [[drag queen]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9zFRRKaWee4 Carisa Hendrix The Woman Behind Lucy Darling]. WERURadio The Urban Sound Of Pride. 11 November 2025.</ref>

== Performing career ==
Hendrix was the subject of the 2016 [[Super Channel (Canadian TV channel)|Super Channel]] documentary ''Girl on Fire.''<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/calgary/carisa-hendrix-girl-on-fire-1.3801795 |title=Calgary fire eater Carisa Hendrix stars in new documentary Girl on Fire |date=2016-10-12 |author=CBC News |author-link=CBC News |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]]}}</ref>

Hendrix has been profiled in major media for their success in [[Magic (illusion)|magic]], a field which has historically been male dominated.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/society/article/hey-presto-the-rise-of-female-magicians-5sqt89mh0 |title=Hey presto . . . the rise of female magicians |last=Malvern |first=Jack |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=2019-04-01 |publisher=The Sunday Times|access-date=2019-08-25 |issn=0140-0460}}</ref><ref name="whosthat"/><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ozy.com/fast-forward/this-is-for-real-how-women-are-crashing-the-male-dominated-world-of-magic/91260 |title=It's No Trick: Women Are Crashing the Male-Dominated World of Magic |last=Bhattacharya |first=Tania |website=OZY |access-date=2019-08-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lotl.com/Culture/Award-Winning-Female-Comedy-Magician-Lucy-Darling-2302/ |title=Award Winning Female Comedy Magician Lucy Darling |website=www.lotl.com |access-date=2019-08-25 |archive-date=2019-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190825115513/http://www.lotl.com/Culture/Award-Winning-Female-Comedy-Magician-Lucy-Darling-2302/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Hendrix has been featured repeatedly at the [[Melbourne]] Magic Festival.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/magic-is-having-a-moment-mixing-comedy-and-music-with-the-art-of-illusion-20180613-h11bgh.html |title=Magic is having a moment, mixing comedy and music with the art of illusion |last=Brookfield |first=Joanne |date=June 23, 2018 |publisher=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=2019-08-25}}</ref>

In 2019, Hendrix was named [[artist-in-residence]] at the Chicago Magic Lounge and appeared on the ''[[Penn & Teller: Fool Us|Penn and Teller: Fool Us]]'' television show.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/chicago/article/Chicago-Magic-Lounge-Announces-Next-Show-In-The-Artist-In-Residence-Series-20190805 |title=Chicago Magic Lounge Announces Next Show In The Artist-In-Residence Series |author=BWW News Desk |date=2019-08-05 |publisher=Broadway World |website=broadwayworld.com |access-date=2019-08-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/theater/reviews/ct-ent-lucy-magic-lounge-review-1101-20191031-qlncpe3jvvhefp53gis5roo75m-story.html |title=Here's a new twist on magic: 'Lucy Darling' does tricks with cocktails at Chicago Magic Lounge |last=Jones |first=Chris |date=2019-10-31 |publisher=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=2019-11-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hicks |first=Glenn |title=P.A.-raised woman makes magical moves |url=https://panow.com/2019/10/01/p-a-raised-woman-makes-magical-moves/ |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=paNOW |language=en}}</ref>

In 2020, Hendrix was featured in the [[Calgary Herald]] "Celebrating 20 inspiring and compelling Calgarians."<ref name=":0" />

As of October 2025, Hendrix has 1.5 million [[TikTok]] followers.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Katsilometes |first=John |last2= |first2= |date=2025-10-24 |title=‘TikTok famous’ not enough for Las Vegas performer |url=https://neon.reviewjournal.com/kats/tiktok-famous-not-enough-for-las-vegas-performer-3323189/ |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=Neon |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[File:Carisa Hendrix during a pre-show talkback.jpg|thumb|Hendrix during a pre-show talkback]]

In December 2025, Hendrix performed at the [[MGM Grand Las Vegas]] Underground Theatre with [[Sarah Hester Ross]].<ref name=":4" />

Hendrix is a regular performer at [[The Magic Castle]], in Hollywood, California, performing as Lucy Darling, the Mistress of Magic: a sharp-tongued, comedic magician partly based on [[Dorothy Parker]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name="whosthat">{{Cite news |url=https://calgaryherald.com/entertainment/local-arts/whos-that-girl-calgary-magician-carisa-hendrix-and-the-rise-of-lucy-darling |title=Who's that girl? Calgary magician Carisa Hendrix and the rise of Lucy Darling |work=[[Calgary Herald]] |date=2019-02-08 |first=Eric |last=Volmers |access-date=2019-08-25}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2012, Hendrix set the [[Guinness World Record]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theyyscene.com/2012/10/25/ffwd-carisa-hendrix-fire-eater-and-world-record-holder/|title=Carisa Hendrix Fire eater and world record holder|last=Anderson|first=Drew|date=October 25, 2012|publisher=TheYYSCENE|access-date=August 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190825110104/https://theyyscene.com/2012/10/25/ffwd-carisa-hendrix-fire-eater-and-world-record-holder/ |archive-date=August 25, 2019}}</ref> for torch teething,<ref>{{cite web |title=Torch Teething World Record |url=https://www.carisahendrix.com/blog/new-guinness-world-record-its-official |access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref> which was featured in both the ''[[Guinness Book of World Records]]'' in 2014, and ''[[Ripley's Believe it or Not!]]'' in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carisa Hendrix |url=https://www.bnientertainment.com/performer/carisa-hendrix/ |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=BigNightIn Entertainment |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> The fire was held in their mouth for two minutes and one second.<ref name=":2" />

In 2017, Hendrix won the [[Melbourne International Comedy Festival Award]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://melbournemagicfestival.com/2017-winners/|title=Melbourne Magic Festival 2017 Winners|date=2017|publisher=The Melbourne Magic Festival™|access-date=2019-08-25}}</ref> and the Award for Best Comedy Show at The Melbourne Magic Festival.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://australianinstituteofmagic.org/ai1ec_event/spellbinder-new-laneway-show-tim-ellis-4/|title=Carisa Hendrix - Up Close & Personal|publisher=Australian Institute of Magic|access-date=August 25, 2019}}</ref> In 2019, they won the [[Allan Slaight|Slaight Family Foundation]]'s Canadian Rising Star Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://melbournemagicfestival.com/allan-slaight-award-carisa-hendrix/|title=Allan Slaight Award - Carisa Hendrix|date=June 25, 2019|publisher=The Melbourne Magic Festival™|access-date=August 25, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.magicana.com/news/blog/canadian-rising-star-2019|title=Canadian Rising Star 2019|author=Julie Eng|date=June 4, 2019|publisher=Magicana|access-date=August 25, 2019}}</ref>

{{Short description|American football player and coach (born 1990)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=May 2026}} {{Infobox gridiron football biography | name = Daniel Sorensen | image = Daniel Sorensen 2021 (51616123844) (cropped).jpg | caption = Sorensen with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in 2021 | current_team = BYU Cougars | position = Assistant safeties coach | career_number = 49, 25 | career_position = [[Safety (gridiron football position)|Safety]] | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|mf=yes|1990|3|5}} | birth_place = [[Riverside, California]], U.S. | death_date = | death_place = | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 2 | weight_lbs = 208 | high_school = [[Colton High School (California)|Colton]] ([[Colton, California]]) | college = [[BYU Cougars football|BYU]] (2008, 2011–2013) | undraftedyear = 2014 | teams = * [[Kansas City Chiefs]] ({{NFL Year|2014|2021}}) * [[New Orleans Saints]] ({{NFL Year|2022|2023}}) | pastcoaching = * [[BYU Cougars football|BYU]] (2026–present)
Assistant safeties coach | status = | highlights = * [[Super Bowl champion]] ([[Super Bowl LIV|LIV]]) | statweek = | statseason = | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 432 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sacks|Sacks]] | statvalue2 = 4.5 | statlabel3 = [[Fumble|Forced fumbles]] | statvalue3 = 4 | statlabel4 = [[Fumble|Fumble recoveries]] | statvalue4 = 4 | statlabel5 = [[Pass deflections]] | statvalue5 = 36 | statlabel6 = [[Interceptions]] | statvalue6 = 14 | statlabel7 = [[Touchdown|Defensive touchdowns]] | statvalue7 = 4 | pfr = SoreDa01 }} '''Daniel Sorensen''' (born March 5, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[BYU Cougars football|BYU Cougars]]. ==College career== Leaving his home state of California, Sorensen became a four-year letterwinner at [[Brigham Young University]].{{cite web | title=Daniel Sorensen | website=BYU Cougars Athletics | url=https://byucougars.com/sports/football/roster/player/daniel-sorensen | access-date=May 6, 2026}} He played in 51 games, recording 211 tackles (122 solo), 1.0 sack (-9 yards), eight interceptions returned for 81 yards and one touchdown, a school-record 23 passes defensed, two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries. Sorensen was named a team captain and earned first-team Phil Steele All-Independent honors as a senior. ==Professional career== On May 11, 2014, the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] signed Sorensen to a two-year, [[United States dollar|$]]930,000 [[contract]] after he went [[undrafted]] during the [[2014 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |last=Thorman |first=Chris |date=May 12, 2014 |title=KC Chiefs sign six undrafted free agents after 2014 NFL Draft |url=http://www.arrowheadpride.com/2014/5/12/5711224/kansas-city-chiefs-undrafted-free-agent-signings-official-list |access-date=December 25, 2016 |website=Arrowhead Pride|publisher=SB Nation}}{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Daniel Sorensen contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/daniel-sorensen-14953/ |access-date=April 9, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}} After going undrafted, Sorensen received calls and offers from multiple teams, but stated he chose to accept the Chiefs' offer because they showed they really wanted him by having head coach Andy Reid call him personally. {{external media | video1 = [http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-combine/0ap2000000331923/2014-Combine-workout-Daniel-Sorensen Sorensen's NFL Combine workout] }} {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 1 3/8 | weight = 205 | dash = 4.54 | ten split = 1.64 | twenty split = 2.64 | shuttle = 3.95 | cone drill = 6.47 | vertical = 32.0 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 2 | bench = 13 | wonderlic = | arm span = 31 | hand span = 8 1/2 | wingspan ft = 6 | wingspan in = 2 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]/[[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |last=Nawrocki |first=Nolan |title=Daniel Sorensen Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/daniel-sorensen/3200534f-5218-1831-f9bb-352a6148cd51 |access-date=April 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}{{Cite web |url=http://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=84451&DraftYear=2014 |title=Daniel Sorensen, Brigham Young, SS, 2014 NFL Draft Scout, NCAA College Football |website=DraftScout.com |access-date=November 21, 2021}} }} ===Kansas City Chiefs=== ====2014==== Throughout training camp, he competed for a roster spot as a backup safety against [[Sanders Commings]], [[Jerron McMillian]], and Malcolm Bronson.{{Cite web |last=Sobleski |first=Brent |date=July 7, 2014 |title=10 Undrafted Free Agents with the Best Chance of Making an NFL Roster |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2518700-10-undrafted-free-agents-with-the-best-chance-of-making-an-nfl-roster |access-date=April 9, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com}} He received an opportunity to display his ability after Commings aggravated a foot injury and missed the majority of training camp. He went on to start three preseason games at strong safety after [[Eric Berry]] sustained an injury to his heel. Head coach [[Andy Reid]] named Sorensen the backup strong safety, behind Eric Berry, to begin the regular season.{{Cite web |last=Vousoughian |first=Farzin |date=September 1, 2014 |title=Kansas City Chiefs 2014 Virtual Program: Depth Chart Analysis, X-Factors & More |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2183086-kansas-city-chiefs-2014-virtual-program-depth-chart-analysis-x-factors-more |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=BleacherReport.com}} He made his professional regular season debut in the [[2014 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs']] season-opener against the [[2014 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] and recorded his first career tackle on [[Coty Sensabaugh]] after Sensabaugh recovered a fumble by Titans' kick returner [[Leon Washington]] during a Titans' kick return in the second quarter of their 16–10 loss.{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Kansas City Chiefs - September 7th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409070kan.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} On September 9, 2014, Sorensen was waived by the Kansas City Chiefs and was signed to the practice squad two days later. It was reported his demotion to practice squad was due to two blunders on special teams that resulted in a failed fake punt and an offsides penalty during their 24–10 victory against the [[2014 New York Jets season|New York Jets]].{{Cite web |last=Thorman |first=Joel |date=September 11, 2014 |title=Chiefs add Daniel Sorensen to practice squad, cut Kona Schwenke |url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2014/9/11/6135501/chiefs-daniel-sorensen-practice-squad-kona-schwenke |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=arrowheadpride.com}} He was promoted back to the active roster on November 1, 2014.{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=November 1, 2014 |title=Chiefs elevate S Daniel Sorensen from practice quad |url=http://www.chiefsdigest.com/chiefs-elevate-s-daniel-sorensen-from-practice-squad/ |access-date=December 25, 2016 |website=ChiefsDigest.com}} On December 28, 2014, Sorensen recorded a season-high two solo tackles in the Chiefs' 19–7 victory against the [[2014 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]].{{Cite web |title=San Diego Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs - December 28th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412280kan.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He finished his rookie season with seven combined tackles (six solo) in nine games and zero starts and was a consistent contributor on special teams.{{Cite web |title=Daniel Sorensen 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SoreDa01/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} ====2015==== Sorensen entered training camp competing for a roster spot as a backup safety against Sanders Commings, [[Kelcie McCray]], and [[Justin Cox]].{{Cite web |last=Tilson |first=Alec |date=August 26, 2015 |title=KC Chiefs: Safety Position Battle |url=https://www.kckingdom.com/2015/08/26/kc-chiefs-safety-position-battles/ |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=KC Kingdom|publisher=FanSided}} Defensive coordinator [[Bob Sutton (American football)|Bob Sutton]] named Sorensen the third free safety on the depth chart to start the 2015 regular season, behind starter [[Husain Abdullah]] and [[Eric Berry]].{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs Depth Chart: 09/01/2014 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/175/KC |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}} He was also named the starting punt protector by special teams coach [[Dave Toub]].{{Cite web |last=Kerkoff |first=Blair |date=August 10, 2015 |title=Perseverance pays for Chiefs' Daniel Sorensen as safety fights for roster spot in 2015 |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article30629223.html |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=kansascity.com}} In Week 10, Sorensen recorded three solo tackles and his first career pass deflection during a 29–13 victory at the [[2015 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]].{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Denver Broncos - November 15th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511150den.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} On December 6, 2015, Sorensen made combined tackles and his first career sack on quarterback [[Derek Carr]] in the Chiefs' 34–20 victory at the [[2015 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] in Week 13.{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Oakland Raiders - December 6th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512060rai.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He finished the {{NFL Year|2015}} season with 23 combined tackles (20 solo), two pass deflections, and a sack in 16 games and zero starts.{{Cite web |title=Daniel Sorensen 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SoreDa01/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} The [[2015 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] finished second in the [[AFC West]] with an 11–5 record.{{Cite web |title=2015 Kansas City Chiefs Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2015.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} On January 9, 2016, Sorensen appeared in his first career playoff game as the Chiefs routed the [[2015 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]] 30–0 in the AFC Wildcard Game.{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Kansas City Chiefs at Houston Texans - January 9th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601090htx.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} The following week, he made one tackle in during a 27–20 loss at the [[2015 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in the AFC Divisional round.{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round - Kansas City Chiefs at New England Patriots - January 16th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601160nwe.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} ====2016==== During OTA's and training camp, Sorensen competed for a role as a backup safety against [[Jamell Fleming]], [[Eric Murray (American football)|Eric Murray]], Shakiel Randolph, [[Stevie Brown]], and [[Akeem Davis]].{{Cite web |last=Thorman |first=Joe |date=August 15, 2016 |title=Chiefs depth chart moves Nick Foles to No. 2 quarterback |url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2016/8/15/12480896/chiefs-depth-chart-moves-nick-foles-to-no-2-quarterback |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=Arrowhead Pride|publisher=SB Nation}} Head coach [[Andy Reid]] named him the backup strong safety behind [[Eric Berry]] to begin the regular season in 2016.{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs Depth Chart: 10/01/2016 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/188/KC |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}} On September 25, 2016, Sorensen recorded two solo tackles, two pass deflections, and made his first career interception off a pass by quarterback [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] during a 24–3 victory against the [[2016 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] in Week 3.{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs - September 25th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609250kan.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} In Week 7, Sorensen made six solo tackles, a pass deflection, a sack, and returned an interception by [[Drew Brees]] for a 48-yard touchdown in the Chiefs' 27–21 win against the [[2016 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. His score in the first quarter was the first touchdown of his career.{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Kansas City Chiefs - October 23rd, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610230kan.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Gregorian |first=Vahe |date=October 23, 2016 |title=No coincidence Chiefs' Daniel Sorensen was in right place at right time |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/vahe-gregorian/article110060987.html |access-date=December 25, 2016 |website=KansasCity.com}} The following week, he collected a season-high seven solo tackles during a 30–14 win at the [[2016 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Indianapolis Colts - October 30th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610300clt.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} On December 4, 2016, Sorensen earned his first career start, as a nickelback, in place of an injured [[Phillip Gaines]].{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2016 |title=Chiefs Vs. Falcons: Inactive Players |url=http://chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-vs-Falcons-Inactive-Players/e75b7070-7ae9-4db3-ae69-705de12f57f2 |access-date=April 10, 2018 |website=chiefs.com |archive-date=April 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180411174255/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-vs-Falcons-Inactive-Players/e75b7070-7ae9-4db3-ae69-705de12f57f2 |url-status=dead }} He recorded five combined tackles and broke up a pass in a 29–28 victory at the [[2016 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]].{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons - December 4th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612040atl.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} In Week 14, Sorensen collected a season-high eight combined tackles during a 21–13 victory against the [[2016 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]].{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at Kansas City Chiefs - December 8th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612080kan.htm |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He finished the {{NFL Year|2016}} season with 63 combined tackles (55 solo), six pass deflections, three interceptions, a sack, and a touchdown in 16 games and one start.{{Cite web |title=Daniel Sorensen 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SoreDa01/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=May 6, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} ====2017==== On March 11, 2017, the Kansas City Chiefs signed Sorensen to a four-year, $16 million contract extension that includes a $4 million [[signing bonus]].{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 11, 2017 |title=Chiefs extend safety Daniel Sorensen |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/03/11/chiefs-extend-safety-daniel-sorensen/ |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}} He entered training camp slated as a backup safety, but saw minor competition from Eric Murray, [[Steven Terrell]], [[Leon McQuay III]], [[Marqueston Huff]], and Jordan Stern.{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs '''Richie Mo'unga''' (born 25 May 1994) is a New Zealand professional [[rugby union]] player who plays as a [[Fly-half (rugby union)|first five-eighth]] for [[Japan Rugby League One]] club [[Toshiba Brave Lupus Tokyo|Toshiba Brave Lupus]] and the [[New Zealand national rugby union team|New Zealand national team]].<ref name="Richie Mo'unga Canterbury Player Profile">{{cite web | url=http://canterburyrugby.co.nz/the-team/richie-mo-unga | title=Richie Mo'unga Canterbury Player Profile | publisher=Canterbury Rugby | access-date=1 January 2017 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020100915/http://canterburyrugby.co.nz/the-team/richie-mo-unga | archive-date=20 October 2014 | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="Richie Mo'unga itsrugby.co.uk Player Statistics">{{cite web | url=https://www.itsrugby.co.uk/player_30034.html | title=Richie Mo'unga Player Statistics | website=itsrugby.co.uk | access-date=20 October 2014}}</ref><ref name="Richie Mo'unga ESPN Scrum Player Profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.espnscrum.com/newzealand/rugby/player/194439.html | title=Richie Mo'unga ESPN Scrum Player Profile | publisher=ESPN Scrum | access-date= 20 October 2014}}</ref><ref name="Crusaders 2017 Squad Guide">{{cite web | url=http://files.allblacks.com/comms/2016-ISR/2017_ISR_Squad_Naming_Crusaders-PUBLISHED-01.pdf | title=Crusaders 2017 Squad Guide | website=allblacks.com | access-date=1 January 2017 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703043050/http://files.allblacks.com/comms/2016-ISR/2017_ISR_Squad_Naming_Crusaders-PUBLISHED-01.pdf | archive-date=3 July 2019}}</ref><ref name="Richie Mo'unga Crusaders Player Profile">{{cite web | url=http://crusaders.co.nz/richie-mounga/ | title=Richie Mo'unga Crusaders Player Profile | publisher=Crusaders Rugby | access-date=1 January 2017 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106014228/https://crusaders.co.nz/richie-mounga/ | archive-date=6 November 2023}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Mo'unga was born in Christchurch, to a Tongan-born father and a Samoan-born mother. He was initially educated at [[Riccarton High School]] in his hometown before being offered a scholarship at [[St. Andrew's College, Christchurch|St. Andrew's College]] where he played U15 in 2009 then 1st XV rugby for 3 years and captained them in his senior year (2012). After graduating college, he began playing for Linwood in the local Canterbury senior club rugby competition while at the same time being a member of the {{rut|Canterbury}} Academy.<ref name="Richie Mo'unga Canterbury Player Profile"/><ref name="Richie Mo'unga Crusaders Player Profile"/><ref name="Young gun Mo'unga firing for Crusaders in Super Rugby">{{cite web | url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/rugby/super-rugby/79659062/young-gun-mounga-firing-for-crusaders-in-super-rugby | title=Young gun Mo'unga firing for Crusaders in Super Rugby | publisher=Rugby Heaven | date = 5 May 2016 | access-date=1 January 2017}}</ref>

== Club career ==
He was not named as a full member of Canterbury's squad for the [[2013 ITM Cup]], but in what was just his first year out of school, he was called up to cover injuries and [[New Zealand national rugby union team|All Black]] absences and went on to make 8 appearances during the campaign which finished with Canterbury defeating {{rut|Wellington}} in the Premiership final. He was upgraded to a full squad member in [[2014 ITM Cup|2014]] and played in 10 matches, featuring both at first five-eighth and fullback as Canterbury fell in the tournament's semifinal stage.

He again made 10 appearances as Canterbury regained their ITM Cup Premiership title in [[2015 ITM Cup|2015]] with a 50–20 win over Springboks in the final.

As a result of his excellent domestic showings for Canterbury, Mo'unga was named in the {{rut|Crusaders}} Wider Training Group for the [[2015 Super Rugby season]]. However, due to the presence of the likes of [[Dan Carter]], [[Colin Slade]] and [[Tom Taylor (rugby union)|Tom Taylor]] in the Crusaders backline, he did not get any game time in his first season at Super Rugby level.

Nonetheless, the departures of all three players ahead of the [[2016 Super Rugby season|2016 season]] saw Mo'unga promoted to the full Crusaders squad. He made his debut on 27 February 2016 in a match at home to the {{rut|Chiefs}} and went on to start all 16 matches during a season which ended with Crusaders losing 42–25 to the {{rut|Lions}} in [[Johannesburg]] in the quarterfinals.<ref name="Richie Mo'unga itsrugby.co.uk Player Statistics"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://crusaders.co.nz/news/910-bnz-crusaders-team-to-play-the-chiefs|title=BNZ Crusaders team to play the Chiefs|publisher=Crusaders|access-date=25 February 2016|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304151537/http://crusaders.co.nz/news/910-bnz-crusaders-team-to-play-the-chiefs|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The [[2016 Mitre 10 Cup]] saw him firmly established in the number 10 jersey for Canterbury, as they went on to be crowned New Zealand champions for the 8th time in 9 years.<ref name="Richie Mo'unga itsrugby.co.uk Player Statistics"/>

Mo'unga started in all of his 13 games in the [[2017 Super Rugby season|2017 season]] for the Crusaders. Mo'unga scored 10 points in the 2017 Super Rugby Final in Johannesburg, South Africa against the [[Lions (Super rugby franchise)|Lions]], leading the Crusaders to a 25–17 win and their 8th Super Rugby title.

Mo'unga finished the [[2017 Mitre 10 Cup]] season as the leading point scorer in the competition, scoring 160 points in just 10 games for {{rut|Canterbury}}. In the final against {{rut|Tasman}}, Mo'unga broke the record for the most points scored in a final when he scored 25 points (2 tries, 3 conversions and 3 penalties). He was named Man of the Match.

In 2018, Mo'unga started in 12 games for the Crusaders. This included a Man of the Match performance in the Super Rugby Final played in Christchurch, New Zealand where he scored 17 points to lead the Crusaders to their second consecutive title.

Mo'unga had a poor start to the [[2019 Super Rugby season]], beginning the season with a low kicking percentage.<ref name="'Super Rugby: How Crusaders pivot Richie Mo'unga turned around his goal-kicking'">{{cite web | url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/rugby/super-rugby/114054003/super-rugby-how-crusaders-pivot-richie-mounga-turned-around-his-goalkicking| title= Super Rugby: How Crusaders pivot Richie Mo'unga turned around his goal-kicking | website=stuff.co.nz | date=7 July 2019 | access-date=19 September 2019}}</ref> Despite his poor start to the season, Mo'unga eventually kicked on, finishing the Crusaders "three peat" season as one of the competition's highest points scorers, second only to [[Handré Pollard]] from the [[Bulls (rugby union)|Bulls]].<ref name="'Super Rugby Stats - Sanzar'">{{cite web | url= https://super.rugby/superrugby/competition-stats/#playerstats | title= Super Rugby Stats - Sanzar | publisher=SANZAAR | access-date=19 September 2019}}</ref> Mo'unga scored 20 points in the semifinal, as well as 14 points in the final, which was a win over the [[Jaguares (Super Rugby)|Jaguares]].

On the 5 November, Mo'unga played for the South Island in the [[2020 North vs South rugby union match]].

Since the start of 2020, Mo'unga has become one of the first five-eighth in New Zealand with performances during Super Rugby, leading the Crusaders to [[Super Rugby Aotearoa]] titles in both [[2020 Super Rugby Aotearoa season|2020]] and [[2021 Super Rugby Aotearoa season|2021]] and again in the [[2022 Super Rugby Pacific season]] with the side now having won six years in a row.

== International career ==
Mo'unga was a member of the [[New Zealand national under-20 rugby union team|New Zealand Under 20]] side, which finished 3rd in the [[2014 IRB Junior World Championship]] in New Zealand, where he scored 29 points in 5 games.<ref name="NZU20 squad named for IRB JWC2014">{{cite web | url=http://www.allblacks.com/News/24842/nzu20-squad-named-for-irb-jwc2014 | title=NZU20 squad named for IRB JWC2014 | publisher=All Blacks | date=23 April 2014 | access-date=1 January 2017 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200909033949/https://www.allblacks.com/news/nzu20-squad-named-for-irb-jwc2014/ | archive-date=9 September 2020}}</ref><ref name="Richie Mo'unga NZ U20 Player Profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.allblacks.com/Player/U20/2229 | title=Richie Mo'unga NZ U20 Player Profile | publisher=All Blacks | access-date=1 January 2017 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170101162355/http://www.allblacks.com/Player/U20/2229 | archive-date=1 January 2017}}</ref>

Mo'unga represented the [[Barbarian F.C.|Barbarians]] against [[New Zealand national rugby union team|New Zealand]], on 4 November 2017, at [[Twickenham Stadium]], [[London]]. Mo'unga scored 7 points, scoring the game's opening try and also converting a Barbarian try in the 31st minute.

After the [[Barbarian F.C.|Barbarians]] match, Mo'unga joined the All Blacks for their Northern Tour, having warranted a place in the squad through his performance in the Mitre 10 Cup. Mo'unga was named on the bench for a New Zealand side for a midweek game against a French side. He converted a try by lock [[Patrick Tuipulotu]] after coming on as a replacement in the second half. This match however did not count as an official test match.

Mo'unga made his official test debut on 23 June 2018 against France during the [[2018 France rugby union tour of New Zealand|France test series]] where he replaced [[Damian McKenzie]] in the 69th minute. The All Blacks won 49–14. Mo'unga made his first ever start for New Zealand during Round 3 of the competition, on 8 September 2018. Mo'unga led the All Blacks to a 46–24 victory over Argentina by scoring 16 of the team's points. Mo'unga only missed one kick on the night and lasted the full 80 minutes.

Mo'unga's starting performance against Argentina saw him temporarily overtake Damian McKenzie, as backup to regular starter [[Beauden Barrett]]. This saw Mo'unga feature off the bench against Argentina and South Africa in the final two rounds of the competition. Mo'unga replaced winger [[Waisake Naholo]], in the 51st minute against South Africa, with [[Ben Smith (rugby union)|Ben Smith]] moved to wing, and Beauden Barrett moved into fullback, to accommodate for Mo'unga at first-five. Mo'unga took kicking duties off Barrett, who had missed a drop goal during the match. Mo'unga converted [[Ardie Savea]]'s last minute try, after the 80th minute, winning the game for the All Blacks, making the final result against South Africa 32-30.<ref name="'He didn't panic' All Blacks coaches rave over Richie Mo'unga's heroics">{{cite web | url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/sport/rugby/he-didnt-panic-all-blacks-coaches-rave-over-richie-moungas-heroics| title='He didn't panic' All Blacks coaches rave over Richie Mo'unga's heroics | publisher=TVNZ | date = 7 October 2018 | access-date=8 October 2018}}</ref> Mo'unga finished as one of the highest points scorers of the Rugby Championship, with 24 points. This ranked Mo'unga 6th of all the points scorers.

Mo'unga remained unable to become a regular starter for New Zealand on the [[2018 end-of-year rugby union internationals|2018 end of year tour]]. After replacing McKenzie in the third Bledisloe Cup test, against Australia, in a 37–20 win, Mo'unga earned a start against Japan on 3 November. Mo'unga scored 22 points during New Zealand's 69–31 win over Japan, including his first international try. Mo'unga stayed on for the full 80 minutes, with debutant first-five, [[Brett Cameron]], instead replacing [[Waisake Naholo]], although Utility Back, [[Jordie Barrett]], did kick some goals towards the end of the test against Japan, in which Mo'unga was one of the best performers.<ref name="'All Blacks player ratings against Japan in the Tokyo test'">{{cite web | url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/rugby/all-blacks/108313505/how-steve-hansens-inexperienced-all-blacks-rated-against-japan-in-tokyo-test| title= All Blacks player ratings against Japan in the Tokyo test | website=stuff.co.nz | date=3 November 2018 | access-date=27 December 2018}}</ref>

He made an appearance in every test on the end of year tour, coming off the bench in the final three, which were wins against England and Italy, as well as a 9–16 loss to Ireland.

Named in the All Blacks squad for the [[2019 Rugby Championship]], Mo'unga was named at first-five-eighth after starting fullback Damian Mckenzie was ruled out of the tournament with an ACL injury. The All Blacks starting five-eighth, [[Beauden Barrett]] was shifted to fullback, as part of a continuation of the dual playmaker system, while [[Waisake Naholo]] was dropped from the national setup entirely to make room for Mo'unga and Barrett's combination. After New Zealand's 16–16 draw with South Africa and record 26–47 loss to Australia the Mo'unga and Barrett combination was criticised in New Zealand widely. With many fans and media alike both favouring the experience of veteran Ben Smith at fullback, and 2 time player of the year, Beauden Barrett, at first five-eighth. However, Mo'unga grabbed a 14-point haul against Australia in the second [[Bledisloe Cup]] test against Australia for the year, before being replaced by [[Jordie Barrett]]. The 36–0 win over Australia saw Mo'unga sustain a shoulder injury, which ruled him out for one test, against Tonga.

On 28 August 2019, All Blacks head coach [[Steve Hansen]] named Mo'unga as one of 31 players selected in New Zealand's squad for the [[2019 Rugby World Cup]].<ref name="'All Blacks squad named for Rugby World Cup 2019'">{{cite web | url=https://www.allblacks.com/news/all-blacks-squad-named-for-rugby-world-cup-2019/ | title= All Blacks squad named for Rugby World Cup 2019 | publisher=allblacks.com | date = 28 August 2019 | access-date= 19 September 2019 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903233140/https://www.allblacks.com/news/all-blacks-squad-named-for-rugby-world-cup-2019/ | archive-date=3 September 2019}}</ref> Mo'unga was named as the only specialist first five-eighth in the squad, with the injured [[Damian McKenzie]], as well as single cap All Blacks [[Brett Cameron]] and [[Josh Ioane]] missing out. Mo'unga started at first five-eighth throughout the tournament, winning the man of the match award against Canada. After a solid display against Ireland in the quarter-finals, Mo'unga and the All Blacks were knocked out of the 2019 Rugby World Cup at the semi-finals against England, losing 19-7. Mo'unga was retained at first-five for the third place play off, where he led them to a 40–17 victory over Wales.

== Personal life ==
In 2019, Mo'unga and his partner, Sophie Vieceli, announced their engagement on social media.<ref name="'All Black Richie Mo'unga gets engaged to partner Sophie Vieceli after 'casual date horse riding down the beach'">{{cite web | url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/sport/rugby/all-black-richie-mounga-gets-engaged-partner-sophie-vieceli-after-casual-date-horse-riding-down-beach | title= All Black Richie Mo'unga gets engaged to partner Sophie Vieceli after 'casual date horse riding down the beach' | publisher=TVNZ | date = 29 August 2019 | access-date= 25 October 2019}}</ref> He is the uncle of [[Fiji national rugby union team|Fijian]] [[Fly-half (rugby union)|first five-eighth]] [[Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.pressreader.com/new-zealand/sunday-star-times/20240526/282488598851502 | title="He's been like a big brother figure to us as well" |work=Sunday Star-Times |date=26 May 2024 |access-date=30 May 2025}}</ref>

'''Adam Tzanetopoulos''' ({{langx|el|Άνταμ Τζανετόπουλος}}; born 10 February 1995) is a Greek professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]] for [[Super League Greece 2|Super League 2]] club [[Niki Volos F.C.|Niki Volos]].

==Club career==

Born in [[Volos]], Tzanetopoulos joined the [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] academies at the age of 15. Three years later, he left Olympiacos, signing a contract with [[Niki Volos F.C.|Niki Volos]]. His distinguished playing along with his ability in defensive game attracts the interest of both [[Nikos Liberopoulos]] and [[Traianos Dellas]].

===AEK Athens===
Tzanetopoulos joined [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] in 2013. Tzanetopoulos scored his first professional goal against [[Atromitos F.C.|Atromitos]] in the [[Greek Football Cup|Cup]] in a 3–0 home victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.gr/stili/oi-prwtagwnistes/article/701679/i-istoria-toy-antam-tzanetopoyloy |title=Τζανετόπουλος: H ιστορία του |date=12 February 2015}}</ref> Tzanetopoulos in his first year with the club played in seven [[Gamma Ethniki|Football League 2]] games and also scored in the 2–0 win over [[A.E. Kifisia F.C.|A.E. Kifisia]], which meant that AEK had mathematically secured their promotion to the [[Football League (Greece)|Football League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.aekfc.gr/pld/antam-tzanetopoulos-43105.htm?lang=en&path=-1186570253 |title=ADAM TZANETOPOULOS - Defender}}</ref>

The summer friendly international with the winners of last year's [[UEFA Europa League]], [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] was a step forward in his career. The Andalusians by having the opportunity to check him realized that he is a player with tremendous perspective, therefore they submitted a proposal to AEK Athens on a long-year loan, with a purchase option of €1.5 million,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/Superleague/aek/tzanetopoylos-to-fthhnotero-perioysiako-stoixeio-ths-aek.3623262.html |title=Τζανετόπουλος: Το φθηνότερο περιουσιακό στοιχείο της ΑΕΚ|date=20 August 2015}}</ref> but was rejected. On 4 February 2016, AEK Athens officially announced that the 21-year-old international central defender Tzanetopoulos renewed his contract, for an undisclosed fee, with the club until the summer of 2020, despite the fact that is not among the first priorities of AEK Athens manager [[Gus Poyet]]. ''"I am very happy for that because it was my desire to stay here, now the only thing in my mind is working hard in order to thank the club's officials for having faith in my ability"'', said Tzanetopoulos, whose previous contract with AEK was expiring at the end of next season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sdna.gr/news-english/article/154801/tzanetopoulos-leave-aek-january |title=Tzanetopoulos renews his contract with AEK}}</ref>
On 28 February 2016, in a derby against rivals [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] returned to the squad after almost three months as a late substitute helping his club to celebrate a 1–0 home win.

As of December 2016, it seemed that international central defender/defensive midfielder of AEK Athens would continue his career at Cyprus, on loan since January.
The 21-year-old player  has performed in only one official match during [[2016–17 Super League Greece|2016–17 season]], the one against [[Anagennisi Karditsa F.C.|Anagennisi Karditsa]] for the Cup.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.novasports.gr/podosfairo/ellada/super-league/article/302441/endiaferon-apo-kupro/#.WEh3BFwxR_E |title=Ενδιαφέρον από Κύπρο |archive-date=7 December 2016 |access-date=7 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161207162223/http://www.novasports.gr/podosfairo/ellada/super-league/article/302441/endiaferon-apo-kupro/#.WEh3BFwxR_E |url-status=dead }}</ref> Eventually, on 9 January 2017, he was loaned to [[Iraklis F.C. (Thessaloniki)|Iraklis]] until the end of the season. He finished the second half of the season with 17 appearances and as a result of his solid performances he returned to AEK Athens.

On 26 October 2017, Tzanetopoulos scored after almost 3 years in a comfortable 7–0 [[2017–18 Greek Football Cup|Cup]] away win against [[Apollon Larissa F.C.|Apollon Larissa]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/ellada/GreekCup/parti-prokrishs-gia-thn-aek-7-0-me-ton-apollwna-larisas.4909213.html |title=Πάρτι πρόκρισης για την ΑΕΚ, 7-0 με τον Απόλλωνα Λάρισας|access-date=26 October 2017|language=el}}</ref>

===Apollon Smyrnis===
On 5 July 2018 Tzanetopoulos joined [[Apollon Smyrnis F.C.|Apollon Smyrnis]] on a three-year deal.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/omades/apollonon-smirnis/epishmo-ston-apollwna-smurnhs-ws-eleutheros-o-tzanetopoylos.5252036.html |title=Επίσημο: Στον Απόλλωνα Σμύρνης ως ελεύθερος ο Τζανετόπουλος |access-date=5 July 2018|language=el}}</ref>

===Lamia===
On 29 January 2019, he signed a contract with [[PAS Lamia 1964|Lamia]] on a free transfer,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/omades/Lamia/lamia-tzanetopoylos-h-tetarth-prosthhkh.5425522.html |title=Λαμία: Τζανετόπουλος η τέταρτη προσθήκη |access-date=29 January 2019|language=el}}</ref> but he didn't play until the end of 2018–19 season.

On 28 May 2021, he agreed to extend his contract, until the summer of 2024.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/lamia-ananeose-o-tzanetopoylos-gia-tria-chronia.9245748.html | title=Λαμία: Ανανέωσε ο Τζανετόπουλος για τρία χρόνια | publisher=sport24.gr | date=28 May 2021}}</ref>

==International career==
On 5 October 2015, the interim national coach [[Kostas Tsanas]] called Tzanetopoulos to replace [[Kyriakos Papadopoulos]], who was injured in [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] Bundesliga's game against [[FC Augsburg|Augsburg]], for the games against  [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]] and [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]], for the [[EURO 2016]] qualifiers. This was the first call of the young [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] centre-back.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/ellada/ethniki_elladas/foraei-ta-galanoleyka-o-tzanetopoylos.3700702.html |title=Φοράει τα γαλανόλευκα ο Τζανετόπουλος|date=5 October 2015}}</ref>

Tzanetopoulos make his debut as a substitute, on 11 October 2015, in a dramatic 4–3 win game over [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] for [[Euro 2016]] qualifiers. It was the first and only win of Greece in the qualification round finishing last in the Group F qualifying campaign.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportinglife.com/football/live/match-report/309143/greece-v-hungary|publisher=www.sportinglife.com|title=Greece - Hungary 4-3|date=11 October 2015|archive-date=22 January 2016|access-date=11 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122055713/http://www.sportinglife.com/football/live/match-report/309143/greece-v-hungary|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Alexandra Park''' (born 14 May 1989) is an Australian actress. She is known for her role as [[List of Home and Away characters (2009)#Claudia Hammond|Claudia Hammond]] in the Australian [[soap opera]] ''[[Home and Away]]'' in 2009. She also starred in the [[E!]] drama series ''[[The Royals (TV series)|The Royals]]'' as Princess Eleanor from 2015 to 2018.

==Career==
Park made her acting debut in the Australian television series ''[[The Elephant Princess]]'' in 2011, playing Veronica.<ref>{{cite web |author=Emanuele Manta |title=Elizabeth Hurley is the str **** in the teaser trailer for The Royals |url=http://www.comingsoon.it/news/?source=tvseries&key=32973 |website=comingsoon.it |language=Italian |date=16 May 2014 |access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref>

In 2009, she played [[List of Home and Away characters (2009)#Claudia Hammond|Claudia Hammond]] in the [[soap opera]] ''[[Home and Away]]''. During that time, she appeared in an episode of ''[[Packed to the Rafters]]'' in 2011. She appeared as Sienna in the 2012 short film ''Arc''.

She also appeared in a 2013 episode of the television series ''[[Wonderland (Australian TV series)|Wonderland]]'' as Jodie. From 2015 to 2018, she portrayed Princess Eleanor in the [[E!]] original series ''[[The Royals (TV series)|The Royals]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Nellie |last=Andreeva|title=E! ''Royals'' Pilot Casts Its Ophelia & Princess|url=https://deadline.com/2013/09/e-royals-pilot-casts-its-ophelia-princess-598410/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=January 26, 2015|date=September 27, 2013}}</ref>

Park played a filmmaker in the [[horror thriller]] film ''[[Carnifex (film)|Carnifex]]'', which screened at the [[Adelaide Film Festival#2022: 19−30 October|Adelaide Film Festival]] in October 2022. It was [[South Australia]]n film editor [[Sean Lahiff]]'s directing debut.<ref name=first5>{{cite web | title=AFF announces the first 5 films for 2022 | website=Adelaide Film Festival | date=30 August 2022 | url=https://adelaidefilmfestival.org/aff-announces-the-first-5-films-for-2022/ | access-date=11 September 2022}}</ref> In the film, Park's character and two conservationists encounter a terrifying new species after huge bushfires have ravaged the land. Filmed in [[Kuitpo Forest]], the film has large-scale special effects, and stars [[Sisi Stringer]] and [[Harry Greenwood (actor)|Harry Greenwood]], son of actor [[Hugo Weaving]].<ref>{{cite web | title=The state of science fiction | website=[[InDaily ]]| first=Penelope| last= Debelle| date=7 October 2022 | url=https://indaily.com.au/inreview/film/2022/10/07/the-state-of-science-fiction/ | access-date=9 October 2022}}</ref>

From 2021 to 2026, Park also appeared in Everyone is Doing Great alongside husband James Lafferty.

==Personal life==
Before getting the role of Princess Eleanor in ''The Royals'', Park was diagnosed with [[type 1 diabetes]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/alexandra-park-details-type-1-diabetes-in-memoir-read-an-excerpt/|title=Alexandra Park Details Type 1 Diabetes in New Memoir: Read an Excerpt|first=Emily|last=Longeretta|date=19 May 2021}}</ref> which she discussed in her book ''Sugar High''.

In May 2022, she married fiancé [[James Lafferty]] in [[Hawaii]] after seven years together.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.com/tv/james-lafferty-marries-actress-alexandra-park-in-hawaii/|title=One Tree Hill's James Lafferty Marries The Royals Star Alexandra Park in Hawaii}}</ref> In 2026, Lafferty and Park announced via Instagram the birth of their child, River Jay Lafferty born on 4 December 2025.<ref>Cite web|url= https://www.eonline.com/news/1431041/james-lafferty-alexandra-park-welcome-first-baby | website=eonline.com | access-date=12 May 2026|date=18 April 2026</ref>
