'''Gabriel Fernando de Jesus''' (born 3 April 1997) is a Brazilian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)#striker|striker]] for {{Spanish football updater|Barcelona}} club [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].

Jesus began his senior club career at [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]], where he was voted [[Prêmio Craque do Brasileirão|Best Newcomer]] at the [[2015 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] and finished first in the [[Copa do Brasil]]. In 2016, he won the [[Bola de Ouro]] helping Palmeiras win their [[2016 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|first national league title in 22 years]]. Jesus signed with English club [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in January 2017 in a transfer worth £27 million,<ref name="CityConfirm">{{cite news |title=Man City confirm Gabriel Jesus move |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2017/01/19/manchester-city-welcome-gabriel-jesus/1483615876492 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=19 January 2017 |access-date=19 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170209164805/https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2017/01/19/manchester-city-welcome-gabriel-jesus/1483615876492 |archive-date=9 February 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and won four Premier League titles, three [[EFL Cup]]s, and an [[FA Cup]]. In July 2022, he joined Arsenal in a deal worth £45 million.

After winning 21 caps and scoring 7 goals at youth level, including reaching the final of the [[2015 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] and winning an [[Olympic medal|Olympic gold medal]] at the [[Football at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rio2016.com/en/news/brazil-s-two-gabriels-set-to-light-up-rio-2016-olympic-football-tournament |last=Marché |first=Patrick |title=Brazil's two Gabriels set to light up Rio 2016 Olympic football tournament |publisher=International Olympic Committee |date=13 July 2016 |access-date=17 July 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160805192530/https://www.rio2016.com/en/news/brazil-s-two-gabriels-set-to-light-up-rio-2016-olympic-football-tournament |archive-date= 5 August 2016 }}</ref> Jesus made his senior debut for Brazil in September 2016. He was part of the squads that took part at the [[FIFA World Cup]] in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]] and [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.soccerladuma.co.za/news/articles/international/categories/world-cup-2018/brazil-announce-23-man-2018-fifa-world-cup-squad/294999|title=Brazil Announce 23-man World Cup Squad|access-date=15 October 2019|archive-date=7 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707165833/https://www.soccerladuma.co.za/news/articles/international/categories/world-cup-2018/brazil-announce-23-man-2018-fifa-world-cup-squad/294999|url-status=dead}}</ref> also participating at the [[Copa América]] in 2019 and 2021, winning the former tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/copa-america-2019-final-brazil-3-peru-1-brazil-seals-ninth-crown-gabriel-jesus-sent-off/article28315233.ece|title=Brazil 3 Peru 1: Brazil seals ninth Copa America title as Jesus sees red|date=7 July 2019 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Born in [[São Paulo]], Brazil. Jesus grew up in the neighbourhood of Jardim Peri, in poor conditions as his mother Vera was a single mother to him and his two brothers.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/sportbladet/a/0Exz9o/erik-niva-om-de-ensamma-mammornas-vm-2018 | title=Erik Niva om de ensamma mammornas VM 2018 | date=30 June 2018 }}</ref> After initially playing street football, he joined amateur clubs in the region, his last one being [[Associação Atlética Anapolina|Associação Atlética]] Anhanguera.<ref name="PTD">{{cite web|url=http://www.verdao.net/noticia.php?n=12383|title=PTD fala com Gabriel Fernando, destaque do sub-17|trans-title=PTD speaks with Gabriel Fernando, under-17's spotlight|website=Verdao.net|publisher=Palmeiras Todo Dia|language=pt|access-date=23 February 2016|date=4 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/palmeiras/noticia/2015/01/joia-2015-famoso-na-base-gabriel-jesus-e-fenomeno-do-palmeiras.html|title=Famoso na base, Gabriel Jesus é "fenômeno" do Palmeiras|trans-title=Famous at the youth setup, Jesus is Palmeiras' "phenomenon"|publisher=[[Globo Esporte]]|language=pt|date=1 January 2015|access-date=23 February 2016}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Palmeiras===
[[File:Gabriel Jesus 2015.jpg|thumb|upright|Jesus warming up for [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] in 2015]]

On 1 July 2013, Jesus signed a youth contract with [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]].<ref name="PTD"/> He was also the club's top goalscorer during the year, scoring 54 goals in 48 matches.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

In January 2014, after lengthy negotiations, Jesus signed a three-year contract for Palmeiras with an additional two, with his salary to increase from [[Brazilian real|R$]]15,000 to four times as much in the fifth year; the fee to buy him out from his contract increased tenfold to R$30 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.palmeiras.com.br/noticias/ler/34888-artilheiro-do-paulista-sub-17-atacante-gabriel-jesus-renova-com-o-palmeiras|title=Artilheiro do Paulista Sub-17, atacante Gabriel Jesus renova com o Palmeiras|trans-title=Paulista under-17's top scorer, forward Gabriel Jesus renews with Palmeiras|publisher=Palmeiras' official website|language=pt|access-date=23 February 2016|archive-date=3 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303202143/http://www.palmeiras.com.br/noticias/ler/34888-artilheiro-do-paulista-sub-17-atacante-gabriel-jesus-renova-com-o-palmeiras|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, the deal changed the balance of his economic rights from 75 to 25% in favour of Palmeiras, to 70–30% in favour of his agents.<ref name=estadao>{{cite news|last1=Batista|first1=Gabriel|title=Gabriel Jesus luta para superar a timidez e lidar com fama no Palmeiras|trans-title=Gabriel Jesus fought to overcome shyness and lead Palmeiras to glory|url=http://esportes.estadao.com.br/noticias/futebol,desafio-de-gabriel-jesus-e-se-acostumar-com-os-holofotes-no-palmeiras,1751885|access-date=23 February 2016|publisher=Estadão|date=28 August 2015|language=pt}}</ref>

Jesus scored 37 goals in 22 games for Palmeiras in the 2014 edition of the state under-17 championship, leading to offers from clubs throughout the country and abroad.<ref name="PTD"/> He was first included in Palmeiras' squad for a senior match on 27 August 2014, remaining an unused [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] as they lost 0–1 at home to [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]] in the [[2014 Copa do Brasil knockout stages|first leg of the last 16]] of [[2014 Copa do Brasil|the year]]'s [[Copa do Brasil]]. He did not make any senior appearances during the campaign, as his side was seriously threatened with relegation;<ref>{{cite web|access-date=23 February 2016|language=pt|publisher=[[Esporte Interativo]]|title=Joia do Palmeiras, Jesus acredita ser muito cedo para jogar no elenco profissional|trans-title=Palmeiras' pearl, Jesus thinks it is too soon to play in the main squad|url=http://esporteinterativo.com.br/futebol-brasileiro/joia-do-palmeiras-gabriel-jesus-acredita-ser-muito-cedo-para-jogar-no-elenco-profissional/}}</ref> this decision, took by managers [[Ricardo Gareca]] and [[Dorival Júnior]], was widely criticised by the supporters, who demanded a change for the youngster through a [[petition]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/palmeiras/noticia/2014/12/em-jogo-do-ano-torcedor-faz-abaixo-assinado-e-exige-escalacao-de-joia.html|title=Em jogo do ano, torcedor faz abaixo-assinado e "exige" escalação de Joia|date=December 2014 |trans-title=In game of the year, supporters create petition and "demand" pearl in the line-up|publisher=Globo Esporte|language=pt|access-date=23 February 2016}}</ref>

Jesus made his senior debut on 7 March 2015 in the season's [[Campeonato Paulista]], replacing [[Leandro Pereira]] in the 73rd minute of a 1–0 win over [[CA Bragantino]] at [[Allianz Parque]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gabriel Jesus estreia, e Palmeiras vence 6ª seguida|trans-title=Gabriel Jesus debuts, and Palmeiras win for the 6th consecutive time|url=http://esportes.terra.com.br/futebol/estaduais/campeonato-paulista/gabriel-jesus-estreia-e-palmeiras-vence-6-seguida,629a4135166fb410VgnVCM10000098cceb0aRCRD.html|access-date=23 February 2016|publisher=Terra|date=7 March 2015|language=pt|archive-date=27 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170727122925/http://esportes.terra.com.br/futebol/estaduais/campeonato-paulista/gabriel-jesus-estreia-e-palmeiras-vence-6-seguida,629a4135166fb410VgnVCM10000098cceb0aRCRD.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He totalled eight appearances, all off the bench, as the ''Verdão'' lost on a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] in [[2015 Campeonato Paulista|the final]] against [[Santos FC|Santos]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} Jesus made his first career start on 29 April in the [[2015 Copa do Brasil Second Round|second leg of the second round]] of [[2015 Copa do Brasil|the year's cup]], a 1–1 draw at [[Sampaio Corrêa Futebol Clube|Sampaio Corrêa]] (6–2 aggregate). On 9 May, he made his first appearance in the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]], starting in a 2–2 home draw against Atlético Mineiro on the first day of [[2015 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Ribeiro Júnior|first1=Ronaldo|title=Rafael Marques marca no último minuto e Verdão arranca empate contra o Galo|trans-title=Rafael Marques scores in the last minute and the ''Verdão'' start with a draw against the ''Galo''|url=http://www.goal.com/br/match/palmeiras-vs-atl%C3%A9tico-mg/2015177/report|access-date=23 February 2016|work=Goal (website)|date=9 May 2015|language=pt}}</ref>

Jesus' first professional goal came in [[2015 Copa do Brasil Third Round|the next round of the cup]], away to [[Agremiação Sportiva Arapiraquense|ASA de Arapiraca]] on 15 July, the only goal of the two-legged tie.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gabriel Jesus marca, Palmeiras vence o ASA e avança na Copa do Brasil|trans-title=Gabriel Jesus scores, Palmeiras defeat ASA and advance in the Copa do Brasil|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/al/futebol/copa-do-brasil/jogo/15-07-2015/asa-arapiraca-palmeiras/|access-date=23 February 2016|publisher=Globo|date=17 July 2015|language=pt}}</ref> On 26 August, his two first-half strikes at the [[Estádio Governador Magalhães Pinto]] gave Palmeiras a 3–2 win over [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] (5–3 aggregate), putting them into the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jogo rápido e show de Gabriel Jesus: como o Palmeiras eliminou o Cruzeiro|trans-title=Fast play and Gabriel Jesus show: how Palmeiras eliminated Cruzeiro|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/palmeiras/noticia/2015/08/jogo-rapido-e-show-de-gabriel-jesus-como-o-palmeiras-eliminou-o-cruzeiro.html|access-date=23 February 2016|publisher=Globo|date=27 August 2015|language=pt}}</ref> Four days later he got his first league goals, starting and finishing a 3–2 win over [[Joinville Esporte Clube]]; the first goal came after 52 seconds.<ref>{{cite news|title=Só Jesus salva! Garoto brilha de novo e põe Palmeiras no G-4|trans-title=Only Jesus saves! Lad shines again and puts Palmeiras into the G-4|url=http://esportes.terra.com.br/futebol/brasileiro-serie-a/campeonato-brasileiro-palmeiras-x-joinville,5b17ed17e986d2605aebeb83bce79b28x4qoRCRD.html|access-date=23 February 2016|publisher=Terra|date=30 August 2015|language=pt|archive-date=2 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160302133330/http://esportes.terra.com.br/futebol/brasileiro-serie-a/campeonato-brasileiro-palmeiras-x-joinville,5b17ed17e986d2605aebeb83bce79b28x4qoRCRD.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Jesus finished the campaign with four goals from 20 games, and his team defeated Santos to win the cup; he was also a starter in both legs of [[2015 Copa do Brasil Finals|the finals]], but being substituted before half-time due to a [[shoulder]] injury. He was elected [[Prêmio Craque do Brasileirão|Best Newcomer]] in the league.<ref name="CBF">{{cite news|last1=de Sousa|first1=Luan|title=Gabriel Jesus é eleito revelação do Brasileiro em prêmio da CBF|trans-title=Gabriel Jesus is elected revelation of the Brasileiro at the CBF awards|url=http://www.palmeiras.com.br/noticias/ler/36891-gabriel-jesus-e-eleito-revelacao-do-brasileiro-em-premio-da-cbf|access-date=23 February 2016|publisher=Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|date=1 December 2015|language=pt}}</ref>

On 4 February 2016, Jesus scored his first ''Paulista'' goal, opening a 2–2 home draw with [[Esporte Clube São Bento|São Bento]] in the second game of [[2016 Campeonato Paulista|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Com gol no fim, Palmeiras sofre para empatar com São Bento por 2 a 2 no Pacaembu|trans-title=With a goal at the end, Palmeiras suffer in order to draw 2–2 with São Bento in the Pacaembu|url=http://www.parana-online.com.br/editoria/esportes/news/932489/?noticia=COM+GOL+NO+FIM+PALMEIRAS+SOFRE+PARA+EMPATAR+COM+SAO+BENTO+POR+2+A+2+NO+PACAEMBU|access-date=3 April 2016|publisher=Paraná Online|date=4 February 2016|language=pt}}</ref> Twelve days later, he scored his first goal in continental football, a 2–2 draw away to Uruguay's [[Club Atlético River Plate (Montevideo)|River Plate]] in the opening game of the [[2016 Copa Libertadores second stage|group stage]] of [[2016 Copa Libertadores|that year]]'s [[Copa Libertadores]], after coming on at the interval in place of fellow youngster [[Erik Lima]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/copa-lib-palmeiras-held-by-river-plate-tachira-down-olimpia-021716|title=Palmeiras held by River Plate, Táchira down Olimpia|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=16 February 2016|access-date=23 February 2016}}</ref> Away to [[Rosario Central]] on 6 April, he scored twice in a 3–3 draw but was sent off for the first time in his career for fighting with Damián Musto; he later apologised for his misconduct.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gabriel Jesus explica expulsão e admite erro: 'Fui infeliz em revidar'|trans-title=Gabriel Jesus explains his expulsion and admits his error: "I was irresponsible to retaliate"|url=http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/campeonatos/libertadores/ultimas-noticias/2016/04/07/gabriel-jesus-explica-expulsao-na-argentina-fui-infeliz-em-revidar.htm#fotoNav=8|access-date=7 April 2016|publisher=UOL|date=7 April 2016|language=pt}}</ref>

In the opening game of the [[2016 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|national season]] at home to [[Clube Atlético Paranaense|Atlético Paranaense]] on 14 May, Jesus scored twice in the second half of a 4–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gabriel Jesus brilha, e Palmeiras goleia Atlético-PR na estreia do Brasileirão|trans-title=Gabriel Jesus shines, and Palmeiras thrash Atlético-PR in the opening game of the ''Brasileirão''|url=http://espn.uol.com.br/noticia/598904_gabriel-jesus-brilha-e-palmeiras-goleia-atletico-pr-na-estreia-do-brasileirao|access-date=29 June 2016|publisher=UOL|date=14 May 2016|language=pt}}</ref> He scored 12 goals as the team won their first national championship since 1994, and was named ''[[Bola de Ouro]]'' for player of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester City-bound Gabriel Jesus earns Brazil's Bola de Ouro|url=http://www.espnfc.com/manchester-city/story/3018497/manchester-city-bound-gabriel-jesus-earns-brazil-league-bola-de-ouro|access-date=20 December 2016|publisher=ESPN FC|date=13 December 2016}}</ref>

===Manchester City===
[[File:Gabriel Jesus fala sobre eliminação do Manchester City Aprendizado 0-2 screenshot.png|200px|thumb|right|Jesus with Manchester City in 2018]]
On 3 August 2016, it was announced that Jesus would sign for [[Premier League]] club [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in January 2017 on a contract until the summer of 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2016/07/25/city-sign-gabriel-jesus/1469474304156 |title=City sign Gabriel Jesus |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=3 August 2016 |access-date=18 August 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817211140/http://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2016/07/25/city-sign-gabriel-jesus/1469474304156 |archive-date=17 August 2016 }}</ref> City paid a reported fee of £27 million/€33 million, plus add-ons.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36964045 |title=Gabriel Jesus: Man City sign Brazilian winger from Palmeiras |website=BBC Sport |date=3 August 2016 |access-date=18 August 2016}}</ref> The transfer was fully completed on 19 January 2017.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Jesus made his first Premier League appearance on 21 January, coming on as an 82nd-minute substitute for [[Raheem Sterling]] in a 2–2 draw with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2017/01/21/manchester-city-gabriel-jesus-interview-tottenham-debut/1485033558304|title=Gabriel Jesus reflects on City debut|date=21 January 2017|publisher=Manchester City Football Club|access-date=22 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202012943/https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2017/01/21/manchester-city-gabriel-jesus-interview-tottenham-debut/1485033558304|archive-date=2 February 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> A week later, Jesus made his first appearance in Manchester City's starting XI, assisting a goal for Sterling in a 3–0 [[2016–17 FA Cup|FA Cup]] win over [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/pep-guardiola-hails-gabriel-jesus-9713159|title=Pep Guardiola hails Gabriel Jesus "the future of Man City" as £27million man bags assist in fourth round FA Cup win|date=28 January 2017|work=The Mirror}}</ref> On 1 February he made his first [[Premier League]] start in place of [[Sergio Agüero]], and assisted [[Kevin De Bruyne]] in the 17th minute and then scored his first goal for the club in the 39th. With this, he became the first Manchester City player to have a goal and an assist in their first Premier League start, as well as only the third City player to be involved in two or more goals in their first Premier League start.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1862/premier-league/2017/02/01/32216682/gabriel-jesus-is-first-man-city-player-ever-to-score-and|title=The Brazil international, who replaced Sergio Aguero in the XI against West Ham, set up the opener before scoring his first goal for his new club|date=1 February 2017|work=Goal (website)}}</ref> In his fourth game (third league start) Jesus broke a metatarsal in his right foot and was expected to be out for the remainder of the [[2016–17 Premier League]] season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39009054|title=Gabriel Jesus: Manchester City forward 'may be out for season'|website=BBC Sport|date=17 February 2017|access-date=19 February 2017}}</ref> However, he returned in April for the [[Manchester Derby]], coming on as a substitute in a goalless draw.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39018821|title=Manchester City 0–0 Manchester United|website=BBC Sport|date=27 April 2017|access-date=27 April 2017}}</ref> Jesus ended the 2016–17 season with seven goals and four assists in 11 games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.premierleague.com/players/19680/Gabriel-Jesus/stats?co=1&se=54|title=Gabriel Jesus Statistics|publisher=Premier League|date=21 August 2017|access-date=22 August 2017|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141744/https://www.premierleague.com/players/19680/Gabriel-Jesus/stats?co=1&se=54|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He scored his first Premier League goal of the [[2017–18 Premier League|2017–18 season]] on 26 August, an equaliser in a 2–1 away win over [[A.F.C. Bournemouth|Bournemouth]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40984015|title=AFC Bournemouth 1–2 Manchester City|website=BBC Sport|date=26 August 2017}}</ref> and added two more in a 5–0 win against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on 9 September.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/41133350|title=Manchester City 5–0 Liverpool|website=BBC Sport|date=9 September 2017}}</ref> He had a 14-game goal drought between 18 November 2017 and 7 March 2018 that encompassed a knee medial ligament injury on New Year's Eve, and after breaking his duck in the Champions League loss to [[FC Basel|Basel]] he admitted that fear of getting injured was affecting his game.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wallace|first1=Sam|title=Gabriel Jesus still playing with fear of being injured again after lay-off|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/03/08/gabriel-jesus-still-playing-fear-injured-lay-off/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/03/08/gabriel-jesus-still-playing-fear-injured-lay-off/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|access-date=23 April 2018|work=The Daily Telegraph|date=8 March 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Jesus scored the last Premier League goal in the 2017–18 season against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the 94th minute, to secure City a league record 100 points.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Johnston|first1=Neil|title= Man City reach 100 point with late goal against Southampton|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44020180|access-date=13 May 2018|work=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2018}}</ref> On 3 August 2018, Jesus signed a contract extension with Manchester City, to take him up until 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/manchester-city-news-gabriel-jesus-contract-a8475541.html|title=Gabriel Jesus signs new Manchester City contract extending Etihad stay until 2023|website=The Independent|publisher=Independent Digital News & Media Ltd|date=3 August 2018|access-date=5 March 2020}}</ref>
On 9 January 2019, Gabriel Jesus scored four goals for the first time in his career against [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] in a 9–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jan/09/manchester-city-burton-albion-carabao-cup-match-report|title=Gabriel Jesus hits four in Manchester City's 9–0 destruction of Burton Albion|last=Stadium|first=Daniel Taylor at the Etihad|date=9 January 2019|work=The Guardian|access-date=20 January 2019|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

On 13 March 2019, Jesus scored once after coming on for Sergio Agüero in the 7–0 (10–2 aggregate) [[UEFA Champions League]] Round of 16 win over [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] and in doing so helped the club equal the record for the largest winning margin in the knockout phase of the competition.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/2019/march/man-city-schalke-record-breakers|title=Manchester City equal Champions League record|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|language=en|access-date=13 March 2019}}</ref> On 22 June, Jesus switched his jersey number from the number '33' shirt to the number '9' shirt.<ref>
{{Cite news|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/2019/june/gabriel-jesus-to-wear-the-number-nine-shirt-for-manchester-city|title=Gabriel Jesus to wear the no. 9 shirt|website=Manchester City|language=en|access-date=22 June 2019}}</ref>

On 7 August 2020, Jesus assisted and scored both goals respectively in a 2–1 win in the second leg of the round of 16 of the Champions League against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], played at the [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]] behind closed doors following the [[COVID-19 pandemic|Coronavirus outbreak]]. Both goals were scored after Jesus' pressing forced two errors from Real Madrid defender [[Raphaël Varane|Raphael Varane]], sealing Manchester City's spot in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{Cite web|date=7 August 2020|title=Jesus leads Man City past Madrid in 8/10 performance|url=https://www.espn.in/football/manchester-city/story/4155362/jesus-leads-man-city-past-madrid-in-8-10-performance-pressing-real-into-mistakes-and-finishing-chances|access-date=12 August 2020|publisher=ESPN|language=en}}</ref> He was the only player to score in two separate games against Real Madrid in the 2019–20 football season, having also scored in the first leg in Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MCFCCityTV|title=Guardiola: Gabriel Jesus the star of the tie|url=https://www.mancity.com/citytv/mens/city-real-madrid-pep-guardiola-reaction-63732417|access-date=9 August 2020|website=mancity.com|language=en}}</ref> This meant he reached 14 goals in only 22 Champions League games, a record bettered by only three non-European players.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gabriel Jesus 14 goals in 22 games statistic|url=https://twitter.com/2010MisterChip/status/1291835942056099840|via=Twitter}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=June 2025}}

On 23 April 2022, Jesus scored four goals in a 5–1 home win over [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], sealing his first [[List of Premier League hat-tricks|Premier League hat-trick]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Bevan|first=Chris|title=Man City 5–1 Watford: Gabriel Jesus scores four as Premier League leaders move four points clear|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61125045|work=BBC Sport|date=23 April 2022|access-date=23 April 2022}}</ref>

=== Arsenal ===
[[File:1 gabriel jesus 2026.jpg|thumb|Jesus with Arsenal in 2026]]
On 4 July 2022, Jesus signed a long-term contract with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], and was assigned the number 9 shirt.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal complete Gabriel Jesus signing |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-complete-gabriel-jesus-signing |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=4 July 2022 |date=4 July 2022}}</ref> The fee and the duration of the contract were undisclosed, yet it was reported the Brazilian signed a five-year contract on a £45 million deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gabriel Jesus Joins Arsenal From Manchester City in £45 Million Deal |url=https://www.sportbible.com/city-xtra/manchester-city-arsenal-gabriel-jesus-transfer-complete-20220623 |publisher=SportBible |access-date=4 July 2022 |date=4 July 2022 |archive-date=15 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220715214521/https://www.sportbible.com/city-xtra/manchester-city-arsenal-gabriel-jesus-transfer-complete-20220623 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 5 August, he made his club debut in a 2–0 away win against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the Premier League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal side look "hungry" after getting their campaign off to the perfect start with victory over Crystal Palace |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62342936|publisher=BBC |access-date=6 August 2022 |date=6 August 2022}}</ref> On 13 August, in his second match and first at the Emirates, he scored his first and second competitive goals for the club against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and also provided two assists in a 4–2 win.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=Adam |title=Arsenal stroll as Gabriel Jesus 10/10 leads win over Leicester |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/arsenal-engarsenal/story/4720218/arsenal-stroll-as-gabriel-jesus-10-10-leads-win-over-leicester |access-date=14 August 2022 |date=13 August 2022}}</ref> On 31 August, Jesus scored Arsenal's first goal in a 2–1 home win over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], helping to maintain their 100% win rate from their opening five matches of the season.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Arsenal maintain their 100% start against Villa |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62655351 |access-date=11 August 2023}}</ref> He was later voted as Arsenal's Player of the Month for August 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 August 2023 |title=Gabriel Jesus is your August Player of the Month! |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-jesus-your-august-player-month |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=Gabriel Jesus is your August Player of the Month! |language=en}}</ref> On 1 October, Jesus played in his first [[North London derby]], and scored from close-range as the Gunners won 3–1 against rivals Tottenham Hotspur.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Arsenal beat 10-man Tottenham to go four clear |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63017880 |access-date=11 August 2023}}</ref>

On 12 March 2023, he made his first appearance since recovering from the knee injury he sustained in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], replacing [[Leandro Trossard]] in the 77th minute of Arsenal's 3–0 win at [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]].<ref>{{cite web|date=12 March 2023|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64852078|title=Arsenal beat Fulham to restore five-point lead|website=BBC Sport|access-date=12 March 2023}}</ref> He scored twice in Arsenal's 4–1 win against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 1 April, his first goals since recovering from his injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65073189|title=Jesus scores twice as leaders Arsenal beat Leeds|work=BBC Sport|first=Matthew|last=Howarth|date=1 April 2023|access-date=1 April 2023}}</ref> He finished his first season with 11 goals and six assists in all competitions.

On 3 September 2023, Jesus scored his first goal of the [[2023–24 Premier League|2023–24 season]] in a 3–1 victory over [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], netting Arsenal's third late in stoppage time.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Arsenal score two late goals to stun Man Utd |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66631567 |access-date=3 October 2023}}</ref> On 20 September, Jesus scored in a 4–0 win against [[PSV Eindhoven]] in the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], as Arsenal made their return to the competition after a six-year absence.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arsenal 4–0 PSV Eindhoven: Bukayo Saka and Gabriel Jesus among goals in perfect Champions League return |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12964871/arsenal-4-0-psv-eindhoven-bukayo-saka-and-gabriel-jesus-among-goals-in-perfect-champions-league-return |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> He then scored in Arsenal's 2–1 loss to [[RC Lens|Lens]] and then again in Arsenal's 2–1 win against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] to become the first Arsenal player to score three goals in his first three consecutive matches in the Champions League since [[Marouane Chamakh]] in 2011.

Jesus scored his first goal of the 2024–25 season on 30 October 2024, opening the scoring in Arsenal's 3–0 win at [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston]] in the fourth round of the [[2024–25 EFL Cup|Carabao Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/oct/30/preston-arsenal-carabao-cup-match-report|title= Preston North End 0–3 Arsenal: Ethan Nwaneri impresses as Arsenal ease past Preston in Carabao Cup|last=Hunter|first=Andy|website=The Guardian|date=30 October 2024|access-date=31 October 2024}}</ref> On 18 December 2024, Jesus scored his first hat-trick for Arsenal, scoring all 3 goals in a 3–2 win over [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in the Carabao Cup quarter-final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/crmnkk2ml1xt |title=Arsenal 3–2 Crystal Palace: Gabriel Jesus Hat-trick sends Gunners into Carabao Cup semi-final |date=18 December 2024 |first=Alex |last=Howell}}</ref> On 12 January 2025, he sustained an [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] injury during a [[2024–25 FA Cup|FA Cup]] match against Manchester United which would sideline him for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/13288445/gabriel-jesus-arsenal-forward-suffers-suspected-acl-injury-in-fa-cup-loss-to-manchester-united |title=Gabriel Jesus: Arsenal forward suffers suspected ACL injury in FA Cup loss to Manchester United |publisher=Sky Sports |date=14 January 2025 }}</ref>

After missing most of the 2025 calendar year, Jesus made his return to playing on 10 December 2025 in a Champions League match against Club Brugge.<ref>Josh James (10 Dec 2025). "Report: Club Brugge 0–3 Arsenal." ''Arsenal.com'', https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Dec-10/club-brugge-0-3-arsenal-match-report</ref> On 30 December, he scored his first goal in over 11 months against Aston Villa, sealing a 4–1 home win for Arsenal.<ref>Matt Hughes (30 Dec 2025). "Gabriel Magalhães’ opener sparks Arsenal’s second-half rout of Aston Villa" ''The Guardian'', http://theguardian.com/football/2025/dec/30/arsenal-aston-villa-premier-league-match-report</ref> After the goal, he celebrated by taking off his shirt, revealing a white undershirt with the words "I belong to Jesus", referencing a celebration first done by Brazilian star [[Kaká]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gabriel Jesus booked for 'I belong to Jesus' shirt as Arsenal make statement win over Aston Villa |url=https://www.gbnews.com/sport/football/gabriel-jesus-arsenal-aston-villa-2674838285 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=www.gbnews.com |language=en}}</ref> On 29 March 2026, Jesus replaced [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]] in the 82nd minute of his side's 2–0 defeat in the [[2026 EFL Cup final]] against his former club [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=Homepage - The English Football League | url=https://www.efl.com/match-centre/g2625816? | access-date=2026-09-18 | website=www.efl.com}}</ref> On 24 May 2026, in the final league game of the season he opened the scoring in a 2–1 win away to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in what turned out to be his final appearance for the club, with the team receiving the [[2025–26 Premier League|2025-26 Premier League]] trophy after the game and Jesus receiving his 5th Premier League winner's medal of his career.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c3d20dk33emt|title=Crystal Palace 1-2 Arsenal: Gabriel Jesus and Noni Madueke score as champions win|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> 6 days later he remained an substitute in the [[2026 UEFA Champions League final]] as Arsenal were defeated in a penalty shootout by [[Paris Saint Germain]] following a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cj6ppx48pk2t|title=PSG 1-1 Arsenal (AET, PSG win 4-3 on pens): Paris St-Germain retain Champions League title|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Jesus made a total of 123 appearances for Arsenal during his four seasons with the club, scoring 32 goals before departing on 1 September 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-jesus-joins-fc-barcelona-aIweE9b0CIaV|title=Gabriel Jesus joins FC Barcelona|first=Arsenal|last=Media|website=Arsenal FC}}</ref>

===Barcelona===
On 1 September 2026, Jesus signed for [[La Liga]] club [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on a three-year contract for an undisclosed fee reported to be €10 million, with a further €4.5 million in potential add-ons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4570072/gabriel-jesus-signs-for-fc-barcelona|title=Gabriel Jesus signs for FC Barcelona|website=www.fcbarcelona.com|date=1 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7550468/2026/09/01/gabriel-jesus-barcelona-transfer-arsenal/|title=Barcelona complete signing of Gabriel Jesus from Arsenal|date=1 September 2026|last1=Cervelló Herrero|first1=Laia|last2=McNicholas|first2=James|website=The New York Times|access-date=1 September 2026}}</ref> On 9 September, he scored his first goal for the club after coming off the bench in a 5–1 victory over [[Feyenoord]] in the opening fixture of the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League league phase]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/uefa-champions-league/articles/gabriel-jesus-scores-first-barcelona-goal-two-minutes-in-on-uefa-champions-league-debut-against-feyenoord-2026-09-09 |title=Gabriel Jesus Scores First Barcelona Goal Two Minutes In on UEFA Champions League Debut Against Feyenoord |publisher=beIN SPORTS |date=9 September 2026}}</ref> A week later he scored his first league goal for Barcelona, again after coming off the bench, adding his side's sixth goal in a 7–2 win over [[Racing de Santander]] at [[Camp Nou]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/barcelona-racing-santander-match-report-7164861-Sep2026/|title=Jesus and Yamal on target as Barcelona cruise to 7-2 La Liga win|author=AFP|date=16 September 2026|website=The 42}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Brasil estreia contra a África do Sul no Mané Garrincha — копия (2).jpg|thumb|upright|Jesus with the [[Brazil national under-23 football team|Brazil Olympic team]] in 2016]]

Jesus was part of the [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil under-20 team]] that finished as runners-up at the [[2015 FIFA U-20 World Cup|2015 U-20 World Cup]] in New Zealand. He scored their first goal of the tournament in a 4–2 win over [[Nigeria national under-20 football team|Nigeria]] in [[New Plymouth]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Brazil triumph in Taranaki thriller|url=https://www.fifa.com/u20worldcup/matches/round=271602/match=300269536/match-report.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150602025942/http://www.fifa.com/u20worldcup/matches/round=271602/match=300269536/match-report.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 June 2015|access-date=23 February 2016|publisher=FIFA|date=1 June 2015}}</ref> and converted as they advanced past [[Uruguay national under-20 football team|Uruguay]] and [[Portugal national under-20 football team|Portugal]] on penalties.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

In 2016, he was chosen in [[Dunga]]'s provisional 40-man squad for the [[Copa América Centenario]] in the United States, and was considered as a replacement for the injured [[Douglas Costa]] in the final selection but missed out through the lack of a [[Visa policy of the United States|US visa]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gabriel Jesus fica fora da Copa América Centenário por falta de documentação|trans-title=Gabriel Jesus remains out of the Copa América Centenario due to a lack of documents|url=http://istoe.com.br/gabriel-jesus-fica-fora-da-copa-america-centenario-por-falta-de-documentacao/|access-date=20 June 2016|publisher=Istoé|date=28 May 2016|language=pt}}</ref> Later that year, he was one of five forward named in the squad for the team's hosting of the [[Football at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Olympic tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rio 2016: Neymar and Douglas Costa in Brazil Olympic squad|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36666740|access-date=29 June 2016|website=BBC Sport|date=29 June 2016}}</ref> He scored once against Danish keeper [[Jeppe Højbjerg]] in their final group game against [[Denmark national under-21 football team|Denmark]], an eventual 4–0 win, and in the semi-final against [[Honduras national under-23 football team|Honduras]] he added two more in a 6–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rio Olympics 2016: Neymar scores after 14 seconds as Brazil reach final|work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/37111213|access-date=18 August 2016}}</ref> Jesus won the Olympics with his team against Germany in a penalty shoot-out, scoring one of the penalties.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/mensolympic/news/y=2016/m=8/news=neymar-s-golden-penalty-sees-brazil-to-victory-2823069.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821102147/http://www.fifa.com/mensolympic/news/y=2016/m=8/news=neymar-s-golden-penalty-sees-brazil-to-victory-2823069.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=21 August 2016|title=Neymar's golden penalty sees Brazil to victory|date=20 August 2016|publisher=FIFA}}</ref>

Jesus made his debut for the senior team on 1 September 2016, in a [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2018 FIFA World Cup qualification]] game against [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] in Quito. He started the match and scored twice, as Brazil won 3–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gabriel Jesus reminds how good Brazil can be in 3–0 win over Ecuador|url=http://www.espnfc.com/world-cup-qualifying-conmebol/65/blog/post/2942340/gabriel-jesus-reminds-how-good-brazil-can-be-in-3-0-win-over-ecuador|website=ESPN FC|publisher=ESPN|access-date=2 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/players-coaches/people=386559/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160407083238/http://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/players-coaches/people=386559/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 April 2016|title=Gabriel Jesus|publisher=FIFA|access-date=12 October 2017}}</ref> Jesus was Brazil's highest scorer in the [[CONMEBOL]] World Cup qualifiers, with 7 goals in 10 matches.<ref>{{cite web|title=Top Scorers World Cup Qualification CONMEBOL 2018|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/world-cup-qualification-conmebol/2018/standingperson.shtml|website=Eurosport|access-date=1 January 2018}}</ref>
In May 2018, he was named in Tite's final [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads#Brazil|23-man squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44116590|title=World Cup: Neymar named in Brazil's 23-man squad|date=14 May 2018|website=BBC Sport|access-date=2 June 2018}}</ref> Jesus started all five games for Brazil at the tournament without scoring a goal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brazil sent packing: Kevin De Bruyne's magic fires up Belgium to knock Selecao out of World Cup |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/07/06/brazil-vs-belgium-world-cup-2018-live-score-neymar-latest-updates/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/07/06/brazil-vs-belgium-world-cup-2018-live-score-neymar-latest-updates/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Telegraph |date=6 July 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

In May 2019, Jesus was included in Brazil's 23-man squad for the [[2019 Copa América]] on home soil.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/138152/brazil-name-copa-america-squad |title=Brazil name Copa America squad |publisher=Football Italia |date=17 May 2019 |access-date=21 May 2019 }}</ref> In the [[2019 Copa América Final|final]] against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] on 7 July, at the [[Maracanã Stadium]], he assisted the opening goal scored by [[Everton Soares]], and later scored the match-winning goal late in the first half; however, he was sent off in the second half after collecting a second yellow card during the final following a collision with [[Carlos Zambrano (footballer)|Carlos Zambrano]]. Brazil won the match 3–1 to win the title.<ref name="2019CAFinal">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jul/06/copa-america-final-brazil-peru-live |title=Brazil 3–1 Peru |work=The Guardian |last1=Smyth |first1=Rob |date=7 July 2019 |access-date=8 July 2019 }}</ref> In August 2019, Jesus was handed a 2-month international ban from CONMEBOL, due to his behaviour after being red carded in the 2019 Copa América Final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/08/08/football/1565260345_314715.html|title=Brazil: Man City's Gabriel Jesus gets two-month international ban|publisher=as.com|date=8 August 2019|access-date=29 September 2019|archive-date=15 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190815181427/https://en.as.com/en/2019/08/08/football/1565260345_314715.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In June 2021, he was included in Brazil's squad for the [[2021 Copa América]] on home soil.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/07/10/football/1625909312_472586.html |title=Brazil national team squad Copa America 2021: selected players, absences... |website=AS.com |language=en |date=10 July 2021 |access-date=11 July 2021 |archive-date=13 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713054036/https://en.as.com/en/2021/07/10/football/1625909312_472586.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 7 November 2022, Jesus was named in the squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Seleção Brasileira está convocada para a Copa do Mundo FIFA Qatar 2022|url=https://www.cbf.com.br/selecao-brasileira/noticias/selecao-masculina/selecao-brasileira-esta-convocada-para-a-copa-do-mundo-fifa-qatar-2022|publisher=[[Brazilian Football Confederation|CBF]]|access-date=7 November 2022|date=7 November 2022|language=pt}}</ref> He was ruled out for the rest of the competition after picking up a right knee injury in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup Group G#Cameroon vs Brazil|final group stage match]] against [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 December 2022 |title=Gabriel Jesus, Telles add to Brazil injury crisis |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/brazil-bra/story/4823870/brazils-gabriel-jesusalex-telles-out-of-world-cup-through-injury-sources |access-date= |publisher=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

==Style of play==
As versatile forward, Jesus has been deployed as a [[Forward (association football)#Centre-forward|center forward]], as an out-and-out [[Striker (association football)|striker]], as a [[false 9]], as an [[inside forward]], as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] or as an [[attacking midfielder]]. Jesus is renowned for his technical skills, [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] ability, creativity, movement, and work ethic. Former Brazilian striker [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] has praised Jesus and touted him for future success with the Brazil national team.<ref name=neymar>{{cite web|url=http://soccerlens.com/gabriel-jesus-the-brazilian-wonderkid-on-everyones-radar/190164/|title=Gabriel Jesus: The Brazilian wonderkid on everyone's radar – Sportslens|date=10 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/sep/30/chelsea-manchester-city-gabriel-jesus-sergio-aguero|title=Gabriel Jesus stars to help Manchester City cope without Sergio Agüero|work=The Guardian|author1=Barney Ronay|date=30 September 2017|access-date=21 October 2017}}</ref> He has been praised by Manchester City's Pep Guardiola 'that of the players he has worked with, he is the ‘best striker/defender’'.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gorrie |first=Jonathan |date=29 July 2022 |title=Pep Guardiola describes Arsenal star Gabriel Jesus as the 'best striker/defender' he's ever worked with |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/gabriel-jesus-arsenal-latest-news-premier-league-2022-b1015397.html |access-date=24 December 2022}}</ref>

In October 2019, Jesus said he was open to switching to a winger role at Manchester City in the hope of getting more playing time, though he acknowledged that there was still intense competition in the team for a starting spot out on the wing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/jesus-open-to-wing-role-at-man-city-despite-having-to-battle/7k1twpvztv6u1483f1m4gdj9r|title=Jesus open to wing role at Man City despite having to battle more than just Aguero {{!}} Goal.com|website=Goal (website)|access-date=21 November 2019}}</ref>

Upon joining Arsenal, Jesus has been placed up-front as a striker in a [[4–3–3]] formation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mehta |first=Utsav |date=8 July 2022 |title=Gabriel Jesus starts a dynamic change up-front for Arsenal |url=https://www.arsenalcore.com/gabriel-jesus-starts-dynamic-change-up-front-arsenal/ |access-date=6 September 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gabriel Jesus came to England with his mother and older brother, along with two friends.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gabriel Jesus: How City's Boy from Brazil Found a Second Family in Manchester|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2816997-gabriel-jesus-how-citys-boy-from-brazil-found-a-second-family-in-manchester|date=12 March 2019|access-date=14 August 2019|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|last=Lang|first=Jack}}</ref> He comes from a religious family and reportedly chose to wear the number 33 in tribute to the age at which [[Jesus|Jesus Christ]] was [[Crucifixion of Jesus|crucified]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jesus could wear Michael Johnson's old Man City shirt number|url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/gabriel-jesus-number-man-city-12251145|date=30 November 2016|access-date=2 February 2017|work=[[Manchester Evening News]]|last=Brennan|first=Stuart}}</ref> He and [[Neymar]] got matching tattoos in August 2016 depicting a boy overlooking a [[favela]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Wright|first=Chris|title=Gabriel Jesus and Barcelona ace Neymar have matching tattoos|url=http://www.espnfc.us/blog/the-toe-poke/65/post/2921757/gabriel-jesus-and-barcelona-ace-neymar-have-matching-tattoos|date=2 August 2016|access-date=6 February 2017|publisher=[[ESPN FC]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=[[Fox Sports]]|title=Brazil teammates Neymar and Gabriel Jesus reveal matching tattoos|url=http://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/brazil-teammates-neymar-and-gabriel-jesus-reveal-matching-tattoos-080216|date=2 August 2016|access-date=6 February 2017}}</ref>

Jesus' signature [[goal celebration]], ‘Alô mãe’ ("Hello, mother" in English) where he makes a telephone gesture – has featured in the [[FIFA (video game series)|FIFA]] video games.<ref>{{cite news |title=UPDATED FIFA 19 new celebrations and tutorial, ft Cristiano Ronaldo, Paul Pogba and Neymar |url=https://talksport.com/football/418292/fifa-19-new-celebrations-cristiano-ronaldo-paul-pogba-neymar |access-date=11 October 2018 |agency=Talksport}}</ref>

Jesus and his partner Raiane Lima have two children, a daughter and son, born in May 2022 and June 2025 respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nasce a primeira filha de Gabriel Jesus e Raiane Lima |url=https://cultura.uol.com.br/esporte/noticias/2022/05/24/3472_nasce-a-primeira-filha-de-gabriel-jesus-e-raiane-lima.html |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=TV Cultura |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lima |first=Melissa |date=2025-06-25 |title=Gabriel Jesus e Raiane Lima anunciam nascimento de segundo filho |url=https://www.bnews.com.br/noticias/esporte/gabriel-jesus-e-raiane-lima-anunciam-nascimento-de-segundo-filho.html |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=Bnews |language=pt-br}}</ref>

'''Celia Jiménez Delgado''' (born 20 June 1995), often known mononymously as '''Celia''', is a former Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right back]]. She made her senior national team debut on September 17, 2014. Celia represented Spain in two [[FIFA Women's World Cup|FIFA Women's World Cups]] in 2015 and 2019, the youngest Spanish player to represent the country in a World Cup. Celia won the 2024 [[NWSL Shield]] and [[NWSL Championship]] with the Pride and was a nominee for the Lauren Holiday Impact Award, honoring her contributions to the community promoting [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] education for young students. She holds a Bachelor of Science in [[Aerospace engineering|Aerospace Engineering]] from the [[University of Alabama]] and a [[Master of Business Administration]] (MBA) from [[Washington State University]] and a cross over to Business from [[Harvard University]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Alcaudete]], [[Andalusia]], Celia grew up playing football at school during recess, leading her mother to encourage her to join hometown club ADV Alcaudete. At the age of 12, Celia was no longer allowed to play on boys' teams and left to join the girls' academy at [[Real Jaén]].<ref name="reinasdelbalon">{{cite web |title=Celia Jiménez, de Alcaudete a Australia |url=https://reinasdelbalon.com/celia-jimenez-de-alcaudete-a-australia/ |website=Reinas del balón |language=es |date=10 November 2019}}</ref> She debuted for the senior team of [[FCF Atlético Jiennense]], Jaén's female affiliate, during the [[2009–10 Superliga Femenina]] season, becoming the youngest Spanish first division player at the age of 14.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celia Jiménez y el temor goleador de los grandes |url=https://www.marca.com/2012/11/29/futbol/futbol_femenino/1354214455.html |website=Marca}}</ref> Ahead of the [[2010–11 Superliga Femenina]] season, Celia joined [[Sevilla FC (women)|Sevilla]] but the team was relegated to the Segunda División at the end of the campaign before winning promotion back to the Primera División the following season. After three seasons, Celia left Sevilla.

===College career===
Celia grew up fascinated by engineering and watched her older sister, Laura, pursue a career in [[aerospace engineering]]. Celia wanted to follow in her sister's footsteps but did not want to give up playing football so, despite fielding offers from clubs in Spain, decided moved to the United States on a scholarship to play [[College soccer in the United States|collegiately]] while studying aerospace engineering.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/espnw/sports/article/21012451/celia-jimenez-delgado-studying-aerospace-engineering-playing-soccer-alabama-crimson-tide |title=Where aerospace engineering and NCAA soccer meet|date=16 October 2017 }}</ref> She spent two years at [[Iowa Western Community College]], helping the Reivers to win the [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] National Championship title as a freshman while being named to the NJCAA 2013 All-Tournament Team and as the Most Valuable Forward in the tournament. She earned first-team All-American honours at the junior college level in both seasons.<ref name="Alabama">{{cite web |title=Celia Jimenez Delgado - Soccer |url=https://rolltide.com/sports/womens-soccer/roster/celia-jimenez-delgado/4048 |website=University of Alabama Athletics}}</ref>

In 2015, Celia transferred to the [[University of Alabama]] to join [[College soccer in the United States#NCAA Division I|NCAA Division I]] program [[Alabama Crimson Tide women's soccer|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. In her first season with the team, Celia made 19 appearances and was selected to the [[Southeastern Conference|All-SEC]] second-team.<ref name="Alabama"/> She suffered a season-ending knee injury in 2016 preseason and considered retiring but, having spent a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt year]] focusing on her studies, returned in 2017 to make 20 appearances and earned All-SEC first-team honours.<ref name="reinasdelbalon"/>

In 2023, Celia earned her [[Master of Business Administration]] (MBA) from Washington State University, complementing her technical background with advanced business and leadership skills. This academic achievement reinforced her ability to bridge the gap between engineering, innovation, and strategic management,

==Club career==
===Seattle Sounders===
On 18 January 2018, Celia was selected in the fourth round (36th overall) of the [[2018 NWSL College Draft]] by [[OL Reign|Seattle Reign]]. In doing so she became the first Spanish player and the first Alabama Crimson Tide player to be drafted into the NWSL.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rolltide.com/news/2018/1/18/alabama-soccers-celia-jimenez-delgado-drafted-36th-overall-by-the-seattle-reign-fc.aspx?path=wsoc |title=Alabama Soccer's Celia Jimenez Delgado Drafted 36th Overall by the Seattle Reign FC |website=Alabama Athletics|date=18 January 2018 }}</ref><ref name="reinasdelbalon"/> She did not initially sign with the team, instead opting to remain in college to finish her degree. After graduating in June 2018, Celia trained full-time with Reign FC while playing for [[Women's Premier Soccer League]] side [[Sound FC (women)|Seattle Sounders]] during the remainder of the [[2018 WPSL season]], scoring the winning goal in the Championship final.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Voght |first1=Steve |title=Seattle Reign FC sign Spanish international Celia Jiménez Delgado |url=https://www.sounderatheart.com/2018/12/12/18138028/seattle-reign-sign-celia-jimenez-delgado |website=Sounder At Heart |date=12 December 2018 |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228025634/https://www.sounderatheart.com/2018/12/12/18138028/seattle-reign-sign-celia-jimenez-delgado |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="2018wpsl">{{cite web |title=Sounders Win 2018 WPSL Championship |url=https://wpslsoccer.sportngin.com/news_article/show/935859 |website=Women's Premier Soccer League |date=22 July 2018}}</ref>

===FC Rosengård===
On 13 August 2018, Celia joined Swedish [[Damallsvenskan]] club [[FC Rosengård]] for the remainder of the [[2018 Damallsvenskan]] season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ericsson |first1=Magnus |title=Celia Jiménez Delgado klar för FCR |url=https://www.fcrosengard.se/celia-jimenez-delgado-klar-fc-rosengard/ |access-date=14 August 2018 |publisher=FC Rosengård |date=13 August 2018}}</ref> She made her debut five days later, starting in a 10–0 win over [[IFK Kalmar]]. She made a total of 14 appearances in all competitions, scoring one goal in a 3–0 win over [[Kristianstads DFF]] on 23 September.<ref name="sw">{{cite web |title=Celia Jiménez – Soccerway profile |url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/celia-jimenez/274193/ |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

===Reign FC===
Ahead of the [[2019 National Women's Soccer League season|2019 NWSL season]], Celia returned to sign with Reign FC.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reign FC Sign Spanish International Defender Celia Jiménez Delgado |url=https://www.olreign.com/news/2019/2/10/reign-fc-sign-spanish-international-defender-celia-jimnez-delgado |website=OL Reign}}</ref> In her first season with the team, Celia made 13 appearances including 10 starts and scored once, the only goal in a 1–0 win over derby rivals [[Portland Thorns FC]].<ref name="sw"/>

During the NWSL offseason, Celia joined Australian [[W-League (Australia)|W-League]] club [[Perth Glory FC (W-League)|Perth Glory]] in November 2019 on loan for the [[2019–20 W-League]] season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Signed, Celia-d, delivered! |url=https://www.perthglory.com.au/news/signed-celia-d-delivered |website=Perth Glory|date=8 November 2019 }}</ref> She made nine appearances and scored three goals.<ref name="sw"/>

With the 2020 NWSL season disrupted by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], Celia played for the newly rebranded OL Reign during the [[2020 NWSL Challenge Cup]] before missing the four-game friendly [[2020 National Women's Soccer League season#Fall Series|Fall Series]] to join [[Division 1 Féminine]] side and sister club of the OL Reign, [[Olympique Lyonnais Féminin|Olympique Lyonnais]], on loan until June 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Celia Jiménez Delgado Loaned to Olympique Lyonnais |url=https://www.olreign.com/news/2020/9/23/celia-jimenez-delgado-loaned-to-olympique-lyonnais |website=OL Reign |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228024130/https://www.olreign.com/news/2020/9/23/celia-jimenez-delgado-loaned-to-olympique-lyonnais |url-status=dead }}</ref> She ultimately didn't make an appearance for the team and was recalled from loan in February to prepare for Reign preseason.<ref>{{cite web |title=El Lyon anuncia que Celia Jiménez regresa a Estados Unidos |url=https://as.com/futbol/2021/02/20/femenino/1613809855_096497.html |website=AS.com |language=es |date=20 February 2021}}</ref> Despite not playing, Celia stated: "Being at OL pushed me to keep growing and developing as a player. I am very grateful for the opportunity both clubs gave to me." Ahead of the 2021 season, Celia also received a permanent resident [[green card]] meaning she no longer occupied an NWSL international roster spot.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kriger |first1=Rachael |title=OL Reign recalls Jess Fishlock, Celia Jiménez Delgado from European loans |url=https://www.sounderatheart.com/2021/2/19/22291147/ol-reign-jess-fishlock-celia-jimenez-delgado-loan-recall-green-card |website=Sounder At Heart |date=19 February 2021 |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228024136/https://www.sounderatheart.com/2021/2/19/22291147/ol-reign-jess-fishlock-celia-jimenez-delgado-loan-recall-green-card |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Orlando Pride===
On 18 December 2021, Celia was traded during the [[2022 NWSL Draft]] along with [[Leah Pruitt]], the 10th overall pick, and a second-round pick in the 2023 NWSL Draft to [[Orlando Pride]] in exchange for [[Phoebe McClernon]].<ref>{{cite web |title=OL Reign Acquire Defender Phoebe McClernon in Trade with Orlando Pride |url=https://www.olreign.com/news/2021/12/18/ol-reign-acquire-defender-phoebe-mcclernon-in-trade-with-orlando-pride |website=OL Reign |date=18 December 2021 |access-date=18 December 2021 |archive-date=18 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211218224650/https://www.olreign.com/news/2021/12/18/ol-reign-acquire-defender-phoebe-mcclernon-in-trade-with-orlando-pride |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 7 November 2024, Celia announced that she would retire from professional football at the conclusion of the [[2024 National Women's Soccer League season|2024 NWSL season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=orlandocitysc |title=Orlando Pride defender Celia announces retirement {{!}} Orlando Pride |url=https://www.orlandocitysc.com/pride/news/orlando-pride-defender-celia-announces-retirement |access-date=2024-11-08 |website=orlandocitysc |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Celia has represented Spain at multiple youth levels, captaining both the [[Spain women's national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Spain women's national under-19 football team|under-19]] teams. She was part of the team that won the [[2011 UEFA Women's Under-17 Championship]], and also finished as runner-up at the [[2014 UEFA Women's Under-19 Championship]].<ref name="Alabama"/>

===Senior===
Celia made her [[Spain women's national football team|senior]] international debut aged 19 on 17 September 2014, starting against the [[Czech Republic women's national football team|Czech Republic]] during [[2015 FIFA Women's World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 2|2015 FIFA Women's World Cup qualification]] but had to be substituted after 25 minutes with an injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vero Boquete pone la guinda al pastel mundialista |url=https://www.marca.com/2014/09/17/futbol/futbol_femenino/1410969038.html |website=MARCA |language=es |date=17 September 2014}}</ref> With only three caps for Spain, Celia was included in the squad for the [[2015 FIFA Women's World Cup]], the youngest player in the squad.<ref name="FIFA 2015"/> She started in all three of Spain's [[2015 FIFA Women's World Cup Group E|group stage]] games in the country's first appearance at a [[FIFA Women's World Cup]]. Spain were eliminated as bottom of the group having lost to [[Brazil women's national football team|Brazil]] and [[South Korea women's national football team|South Korea]], and drew with [[Costa Rica women's national football team|Costa Rica]].<ref name="sw"/>

In 2017, Celia was named to her second successive major tournament squad as Spain contested the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2017]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Convocatoria de la Selección femenina para el Campeonato de Europa |url=http://www.rfef.es/noticias/oficial-convocatoria-seleccion-femenina-campeonato-europa |website=www.rfef.es |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=8 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180208222334/http://www.rfef.es/noticias/oficial-convocatoria-seleccion-femenina-campeonato-europa |url-status=dead }}</ref> She was an unused substitute behind [[Marta Torrejón]] in all four games as Spain were eliminated on penalties by [[Austria women's national football team|Austria]] in the quarter-finals.<ref name="sw"/>

In 2018, Celia was part of the squad that won the [[2018 Cyprus Women's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Spain Announce Squad for the Cyprus Women's Cup 2018 |url=https://www.womenssoccerunited.com/spain-announce-squad-for-the-cyprus-womens-cup-2018/ |website=Womens Soccer United |date=20 February 2018 |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=29 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229210845/https://www.womenssoccerunited.com/spain-announce-squad-for-the-cyprus-womens-cup-2018/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Cyprus">{{cite web |title=¡España, campeona de la Cyprus Cup! |url=https://www.rfef.es/noticias/cronica-espana-campeona-cyprus-cup |website=www.rfef.es |language=es |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=28 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228024315/https://www.rfef.es/noticias/cronica-espana-campeona-cyprus-cup |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2019, Celia was called up for the [[2019 FIFA Women's World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Estas son las convocadas de la Selección española femenina para la Copa Mundial de Francia |url=https://www.sefutbol.com/oficial-estas-son-convocadas-seleccion-espanola-femenina-copa-mundial-francia |website=www.sefutbol.com |language=es |date=20 May 2019 |access-date=28 December 2021 |archive-date=31 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190531021631/https://www.sefutbol.com/oficial-estas-son-convocadas-seleccion-espanola-femenina-copa-mundial-francia |url-status=dead }}</ref> She made one appearance, as an 86th-minute substitute in a goalless draw with [[China women's national football team|China]] in the group. Spain were eliminated in the round of 16 by eventual winners [[United States women's national soccer team|United States]].<ref name="sw"/>

'''Katie Uhlmann''' (born September 1, 1987) is a Canadian interview host, director, actress and writer, most noted for the web series ''[[My Roommate's an Escort]]'' and ''[[Cows Come Home]]''.<ref>Luke Hendry, [https://www.intelligencer.ca/news/katie-uhlmann-tv-film-career-tips "Katie Uhlmann's tip for screen success: find a mentor"]. ''[[Belleville Intelligencer]]'', June 12, 2025.</ref>

Originally from [[Trenton, Ontario|Trenton]], [[Ontario]], she attended [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]], initially with the goal of becoming an [[optometrist]], but switched to dramatic arts after her first year.<ref>Megan Mattice, [https://www.intelligencer.ca/2013/07/25/katie-uhlmann-would-have-been-an-optometrist "Katie Uhlmann: Would have been an optometrist"]. ''[[Belleville Intelligencer]]'', July 25, 2013.</ref> Alongside her early career as an actress she launched the online talk show ''Katie Chats'', with which she completed over 3,000 interviews with Canadian filmmakers and celebrities. In interviewing so many members of the Canadian entertainment community, her goal was to develop a resource for students of the Canadian entertainment community and industry, stating that she has set out to create the largest database of interviews with Canadian talent in the world.<ref name="richardcrouseradiohKK">[http://www.richardcrouse.ca/the-richard-crouse-show-on-newstalk-1010-welcomes-keram-malicki-sanchez/ "Interview with Katie Uhlmann"]. ''[[The Richard Crouse Show]]'', [[Newstalk 1010]]. Retrieved 20 April 2015.</ref><ref name="trentonianjKK">Mattice, Megan(1 August 2013). [http://eedition.trentonian.ca/doc/Trenton-Trentonian/tretonian-august-1/2013073101/8.html#8 "From Trenton to Silver Screen"]. ''[[Trenton Trentonian|The Trentonian]]''. Retrieved 20 April 2015.</ref>  

In 2017, she wrote, directed and starred in the web series ''My Roommate’s an Escort''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/arts/television/john-doyle-online-and-on-tv-april-is-the-coolest-month/article34560607/|title=John Doyle: Online and on TV, April is the coolest month|last=Doyle|first=John|date=2017-04-03|access-date=2017-07-24|language=en-ca}}</ref> She later created ''Cows Come Home'' with [[Lindsey Middleton]] in 2025,<ref>Shilpashree Jagannathan, [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/hamilton/cows-come-home-1.7590244 "New series set on dairy farm in Fort Erie a 'love letter' to rural Ontario"]. [[CBC Hamilton]], July 23, 2025.</ref> which won the [[Canadian Screen Awards]] for Best Original Web Program or Series, Fiction and Best Direction in a Web Program or Series at the [[14th Canadian Screen Awards]] in 2026.<ref name=thiessen>Connie Thiessen, [https://broadcastdialogue.com/heated-rivalry-sets-new-canadian-screen-awards-record/ "Heated Rivalry sets new Canadian Screen Awards record"]. ''Broadcast Dialogue'', May 31, 2026.</ref>

'''Vivienne Horne''' (born March 24, 1991) is a Canadian politician who was elected in the [[2015 Alberta general election]] to the [[Legislative Assembly of Alberta]] representing the [[electoral district]] of [[Spruce Grove-St. Albert]]. She was a student in [[political science]] at [[MacEwan University]] in Edmonton.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://edmontonjournal.com/Riding+profile+Spruce+Grove+Albert/11014885/story.html| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150530015634/http://www.edmontonjournal.com/Riding+profile+Spruce+Grove+Albert/11014885/story.html| archive-date = 2015-05-30| title = Riding results: Spruce Grove-St. Albert: Spruce Grove-St. Albert: Youngster victorious}}</ref>

Prior to her election, Horne was a [[barista]] at a St. Albert [[Starbucks]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/trevor-horne-barista-ready-to-make-transition-to-ndp-mla-1.3079718|title=Slinging coffee and kissing babies: Barista soon to be an NDP MLA {{!}} CBC News|work=CBC|access-date=2018-05-31|language=en-US}}</ref>

Horne came out as transgender in 2025.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://docs.assembly.ab.ca/LADDAR_files/docs/hansards/han/legislature_31/session_2/20251117_1330_01_han.pdf#page=261 |title=The 31st Legislature Second Session Alberta Hansard: Monday afternoon, November 17, 2025 |year=2025 |publication-date=2025 |pages=261}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Horne |first1=Vivienne |title=A (re)introduction |url=https://medium.com/@vivienne.horne/a-re-introduction-32e910b09b3f |access-date=6 February 2026}}</ref>

Horne endorsed Alberta MP [[Heather McPherson (politician)|Heather McPherson]] in the [[2026 New Democratic Party leadership election]].<ref name="WandJan">{{cite news |last1=Wand |first1=Eleanor |title=McPherson’s NDP leadership bid secures most ex-MP support, but Lewis nabs only caucus nod |url=https://www.hilltimes.com/story/2026/01/22/mcphersons-ndp-leadership-bid-secures-most-ex-mp-endorsements-but-lewis-nabs-only-caucus-nod/488722/ |access-date=February 8, 2026 |work=The Hill Times |date=January 22, 2026}}</ref>

'''Mônica Hickmann Alves''' (born 21 April 1987), commonly known as '''Mônica''', is a Brazilian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] for Spanish [[Liga F]] club [[Madrid CFF]] and the [[Brazil women's national football team|Brazil national team]]. She participated in the [[2015 FIFA Women's World Cup|2015]] and [[2019 FIFA Women's World Cup]]s and the [[Football at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2016 Rio Olympics]].

==Club career==
Between 2007 and 2012, Mônica played club football in Austria for [[SV Neulengbach]], the dominant team in the [[ÖFB-Frauenliga]]. Upon returning to Brazil, she had a short spell with [[Botucatu Futebol Clube]], then joined [[Associação Ferroviária de Esportes (women)|Ferroviária]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Confederação Brasileira de Futebol súmula on-line – CBF, jogo 61|url=http://conteudo.cbf.com.br/sumulas/2014/552461se.pdf|publisher=[[Brazilian Football Confederation]]|access-date=14 June 2015|language=Portuguese|date=30 March 2014}}</ref> ahead of the 2013 season.<ref name="guerreiras" />

She then joined the new expansion side, the [[Orlando Pride]] of the [[National Women's Soccer League]] for the 2016 season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.orlandocitysc.com/post/2015/12/08/orlando-pride-signs-monica-hickmann-alves|title=Orlando Pride Signs Monica Hickmann Alves|work=Orlando City Soccer Club}}</ref> complemented by loan spells with [[Adelaide United FC (W-League)|Adelaide United]] and [[Atlético Madrid Femenino|Atlético Madrid]] in the 2016 and 2017 offseasons respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thewomensgame.com/2016/10/brazilian-international-monica-joins-adelaide-united/|title=Brazilian international Monica joins Adelaide United|publisher=The Women's Game|date=25 October 2016}}</ref> On February 18, 2019, after three seasons with Orlando she announced she was leaving the club.

In April 2019, Mônica signed for reigning [[Campeonato Brasileiro de Futebol Feminino]] champions [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista (women's football)|Corinthians]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Corinthians contrata zagueira da Seleção, com passagem pelos EUA |url=https://www.lance.com.br/corinthians/contrata-zagueira-selecao-com-passagem-pelos-eua.html |access-date=24 April 2019 |publisher=[[Lance!]] |date=23 April 2019 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

In August 2019, Mônica signed for Spanish [[Primera División (women)|Primera División]] club [[Madrid CFF]].<ref>{{cite web |title=MONICA HICKMANN ya es del Madrid CFF |url=http://madridcff.com/monica-hickmann-madrid-cff-fichaje/ |website=Madrid Club de Fútbol Femenino |language=es |date=25 August 2019}}</ref>

==International career==
At the [[2006 FIFA U-20 Women's World Championship]], Mônica was part of the Brazilian team which finished third.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Leme de Arruda|first1=Marcelo|last2=do Nascimento Pereira|first2=André|title=SELEÇÃO BRASILEIRA SUB-20 FEMININA (WOMENS' U-20 BRAZILIAN NATIONAL TEAM) 2002–2014|url=http://www.rsssfbrasil.com/sel/brazil200214u20w.htm|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|access-date=14 June 2015|date=28 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710094831/http://www.rsssfbrasil.com/sel/brazil200214u20w.htm|archive-date=10 July 2015}}</ref> She made her senior [[Brazil women's national football team]] debut on 11 June 2014, a 0–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] draw with [[France women's national football team|France]] staged in [[Guyana]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Monica|url=https://www.fifa.com/womensworldcup/players/player=251055/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611111636/http://www.fifa.com/womensworldcup/players/player=251055/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 June 2015|publisher=[[FIFA]]|access-date=14 June 2015}}</ref> She scored her first national team goal in Brazil's 7–1 win over Ecuador at the [[Football at the 2015 Pan American Games – Women's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]]. A controversial own goal by Mônica against [[Australia women's national football team|Australia]] at the [[2019 FIFA Women's World Cup]] saw Brazil lose its first group stage match in 24 years.<ref>{{cite web|title=Women's World Cup: Brazil Lose First Group Stage Match in 24 Years|date=13 June 2019 |url=https://www.news18.com/news/football/womens-world-cup-2019-australia-vs-brazil-historic-victory-2185901.html|publisher=News 18|access-date=14 June 2019}}</ref>

'''Alberto Carlos Rosende III''' is an American actor and singer, known for his role as [[Simon Lewis (The Mortal Instruments)|Simon Lewis]] in the [[Freeform (TV channel)|Freeform]] supernatural drama ''[[Shadowhunters]]'' from 2016 to 2019. From 2019 to 2024, he starred as Firefighter Blake Gallo in the [[NBC]] drama ''[[Chicago Fire (TV series)|Chicago Fire]]''.

==Early life and education==
Rosende was born to Martha Cristina Ferrucho and Alberto Carlos Rosende, a major-general in the U.S. Army Reserve. He has a younger brother, Diego, who works in the film production industry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Maj. Gen. Alberto C. Rosende|url=https://www.usar.army.mil/Leadership/Article-View/Article/1613137/maj-gen-alberto-c-rosende/|access-date=2020-11-11|website=www.usar.army.mil}}</ref> He is of [[Colombia]]n and [[Cubans|Cuban]] descent.<ref name="Bustle2016">{{cite web|url=http://www.bustle.com/articles/135112-who-is-simon-on-shadowhunters-alberto-rosende-is-the-heart-of-the-series|title=Who Is Simon On 'Shadowhunters'? Alberto Rosende Is The Heart Of The Series|website=[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]|first=Leah|last=Thomas|date=January 12, 2016}}</ref> Rosende attended Fort Lauderdale Children's Theater, where he appeared in a number of productions, which included starring as Link Larkin in ''[[Hairspray (musical)|Hairspray]]''. He attended [[St. Thomas Aquinas High School (Fort Lauderdale, Florida)|St. Thomas Aquinas High School]] in Fort Lauderdale, where he was a member of the STA Players. While there, Rosende performed as Danny Zuko in ''[[Grease (musical)|Grease]]'', Emile De Becque in ''[[South Pacific (musical)|South Pacific]]'', and Dr. Lyman Sanderson in ''[[Harvey (play)|Harvey]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2010-03-16/news/sfe-teenlink-harvey1_1_veta-louise-simmons-elwood-p-dowd-judge-omar-gaffney|title="Harvey" recognizes that perhaps no one is really sane or insane|website=[[South Florida Sun-Sentinel]]|first=Jessica|last=Kent|date=March 16, 2010|access-date=2016-01-25|archive-date=2017-07-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170731112340/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2010-03-16/news/sfe-teenlink-harvey1_1_veta-louise-simmons-elwood-p-dowd-judge-omar-gaffney|url-status=dead}}</ref> In April 2013, Rosende was diagnosed with [[testicular cancer]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Bandyopadhyay|first=Alakananda|date=December 11, 2018|title=Shadowhunters' Alberto Rosende is a cancer-beating, swing-dancing, gun violence-protesting fighter|url=https://meaww.com/shadowhunters-alberto-rosende-cancer-beating-swing-dancing-gun-violence-protesting|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190104124040/https://meaww.com/shadowhunters-alberto-rosende-cancer-beating-swing-dancing-gun-violence-protesting|archive-date=January 4, 2019|access-date=November 11, 2020|website=Meaww.com}}</ref> In 2015, Rosende graduated from [[New York University]]'s [[Tisch School of the Arts]] with a [[Bachelor of Fine Arts]].<ref name="Bustle2016"/>

==Career==
Rosende's first professional acting credit was as a swing dancer in the 2013 short film ''The Swing of Things''. In 2015, he guest-starred in the [[CBS]] police procedural drama ''[[Blue Bloods]]'', in the fifth-season episode "Sins of the Father", as Carlos Santiago.<ref>{{cite web|first=Denise|last=Petski|title=Alberto Rosende & Emeraude Toubia Join 'Shadowhunters'|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=May 1, 2015|url=https://deadline.com/2015/05/alberto-rosende-emeraude-toubia-cast-shadowhunters-abc-family-1201419267/|access-date=June 7, 2015}}</ref> That same year, he guest-starred in the [[NBC]] police procedural drama ''[[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit]]'' in the seventeenth-season episode "Catfishing Teacher" as Jordan Messina. On May 2, 2015, it was announced that Rosende had been cast as [[Simon Lewis (The Mortal Instruments)|Simon Lewis]] in the [[Freeform (TV channel)|Freeform]] supernatural drama ''[[Shadowhunters]]'', based on [[Cassandra Clare]]'s ''[[The Mortal Instruments]]'' book series, which ran from January 12, 2016, to May 6, 2019.<ref name="RosendeToubia">{{cite web|last=Ge|first=Linda|date=May 1, 2015|title=ABC Family's 'Shadowhunters' Adds Alberto Rosende and Emeraude Toubia|url=https://www.thewrap.com/abc-familys-shadowhunters-adds-alberto-rosende-and-emeraude-toubia/|website=[[TheWrap]]|access-date=May 1, 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In December 2021, Rosende became engaged to actress and former ''[[Shadowhunters]]'' co-star Tessa Mossey. The couple got legally married in 2022, before having their ceremony in 2025 surrounded by friends and family in Prince Edward Island. The wedding was followed by Hello! Magazine and photos were published in August 2025. <ref>{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Schultz|title=Chicago Fire star Alberto Rosende announces engagement to Tessa Mossey|website=[[FanSided]]|url=https://onechicagocenter.com/2021/12/28/chicago-fire-star-alberto-rosende-engaged-tessa-mossey/|date=December 28, 2021}}
</ref>
