'''Dorothy Wang Yankowitz''' (born January 27, 1988)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Ghai |first=Anahita |date=January 24, 2023 |title=Who is Dorothy Wang, From Bling Empire New York? |url=https://www.harpersbazaararabia.com/culture/celebrity/who-is-dorothy-wang |access-date=October 2, 2026 |website=[[Harper's Bazaar Arabia]] |language=en-US}}</ref> is an American television personality, socialite, heiress, and entrepreneur. Wang rose to fame when she appeared on the [[E!]] reality series ''[[Rich Kids of Beverly Hills]]'' (2014–2016). She later appeared on the Netflix reality series ''[[Bling Empire]]'' (2022).

== Early life ==
Wang was born on January 27, 1988, in [[Beverly Hills, California]], where she was raised.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> The youngest of two children, Wang is the daughter of [[Taiwanese people|Taiwanese]] parents Vivine Wang, philanthropist, and [[Roger Wang|H. Roger Wang]], founder of [[Nanjing]] real estate development group Golden Eagle International, which she is an heiress to. She has one older sister named Janice.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shao |first=Heng |date=October 9, 2014 |title=Big-Spending Daughter Of Chinese-American Billionaire Finds Instafame In Reality TV |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hengshao/2014/10/09/instafamous/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013064533/https://www.forbes.com/sites/hengshao/2014/10/09/instafamous/ |archive-date=October 13, 2014 |access-date=October 2, 2026 |website=[[Forbes]] |agency=Forbes Asia}}</ref> Wang attended the [[Harvard-Westlake School]], where she was a cheerleader and landed her first job in a [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] commercial.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Flora |first=Liz |date=June 8, 2015 |title=Dorothy Wang of 'Rich Kids of Beverly Hills' Talks Chinese Fashion, Social Media, and her '#Fabuluxe' Lifestyle |url=https://jingdaily.com/posts/dorothy-wang-of-rich-kids-of-beverly-hills-talks-chinese-fashion-social-media-and-her-fabuluxe-lifestyle |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=Jing Daily |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Macias |first=Ernesto |date=January 20, 2023 |title=Beverly Hills Who? Dorothy Wang Loves New York |url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/television/beverly-hills-who-dorothy-wang-is-a-new-york-city-girl |access-date=October 3, 2024 |website=[[Interview (magazine)|Interview]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Wang attended both [[University of Southern California]] and [[Southern Methodist University]] before ultimately graduating from USC.<ref name=":3" /> According to Wang, she wasn't aware of her families wealth until she discovered her father on a ''[[Forbes]]'' list when she was an adult.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Rich Kids of Beverly Hills |url=https://www.flaunt.com/blog/people-birkins-speak-rich-kids-beverly-hills |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=Flaunt Magazine}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2012, Wang, then-24, began being featured on the [[Tumblr]] website "The Rich Kids of Instagram", where she was discovered by television producers who approached her to appear in an upcoming reality series based on the blog. After recommending friend Morgan Stewart, the two recruited friends for casting.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisman |first=Aly |date=November 6, 2014 |title=How A Billionaire Heiress Ended Up Joining 'Rich Kids Of Beverly Hills' |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/how-dorothy-wang-cast-rich-kids-beverly-hills-2014-11 |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[Business Insider]] |language=en-US}}</ref> By August 2013, it was announced that [[E! Network]] was developing ''[[Rich Kids of Beverly Hills]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=August 5, 2013 |title=E! Developing 'Rich Kids Of Beverly Hills' Reality Series |url=https://deadline.com/2013/08/e-developing-rich-kids-of-beverly-hills-reality-series-556936/ |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In October, Wang, along with the ensemble cast were announced as the show's main subjects.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Connell |first=Mikey |date=October 17, 2013 |title=E! Orders 'Rich Kids of Beverly Hills' to Series |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/e-orders-rich-kids-beverly-649306/ |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Upon its January 2014 airing, Wang, like the rest of the cast, received widespread media attention from critics including [[Jon Caramanica]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'', who referred to the cast as "young narcissists relentlessly documenting themselves."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Caramanica |first=Jon |author-link=Jon Caramanica |date=January 17, 2014 |title=Pop on Those Prada Shades, Puff Out Your Lips and Say, 'Puh-leeeze!' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/01/18/arts/television/rich-kids-of-beverly-hills-self-chronicle-of-privileged-youth.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140131200744/https://www.nytimes.com/2014/01/18/arts/television/rich-kids-of-beverly-hills-self-chronicle-of-privileged-youth.html |archive-date=January 31, 2014 |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> Nonetheless, Wang remained a main cast member for four seasons until the show's cancellation in November 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lefkowitz |first=Emily |date=November 3, 2016 |title='Rich Kids of Beverly Hills' Canceled After Four Seasons |url=https://www.etonline.com/tv/201974_exclusive_rich_kids_of_beverly_hills_canceled_after_four_seasons |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[Entertainment Tonight]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Also in November 2016, Wang was announced as a cast member on the second season of E!'s reality dating series ''[[Famously Single]]'', which aired in June 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=November 2, 2016 |title='Famously Single' Renewed For Season 2 By E! With Karina Smirnoff, More |url=https://deadline.com/2016/11/famously-single-renewed-season-2-e-karina-smirnoff-chad-johnson-1201847495/ |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2017, Wang announced the launch of her short-lived champagne line "Rich and Bubbly", which was sold on her website.<ref name=":2" />

In April 2022, Wang joined the cast of [[Netflix]]'s reality series ''[[Bling Empire]]'' for its second season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trainor |first=Daniel |date=April 15, 2022 |title=Meet Bling Empire's 2 New Cast Members For Season 2 |url=https://www.eonline.com/ca/news/1327412/meet-bling-empires-2-new-cast-members-for-season-2 |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[E! Online]]}}</ref> Wang was then announced as a part of the cast for the show's spin off, ''Bling Empire: New York'', which premiered in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trainor |first=Daniel |date=December 13, 2022 |title=Bling Empire: New York Has a Premiere Date & a Hilarious New Sneak Peek Starring Dorothy Wang |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1358028/bling-empire-new-york-has-a-premiere-date-a-hilarious-new-sneak-peek-starring-dorothy-wang |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[E! Online]]}}</ref> In April, both series were canceled.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yam |first=Kimmy |date=April 21, 2023 |title=Netflix cancels 'Bling Empire' and its spinoff |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/asian-america/netflix-cancels-bling-empire-spinoff-rcna80849 |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[NBC News]] |language=en}}</ref> In September 2026, Wang launched her five-part wedding docuseries ''Dorothy's I Do'', co-produced by Wang and her husband's production company Chez Yankowitz, along with former ''Rich Kids of Beverly Hills'' producer Gennifer Gardiner.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Peter |date=September 11, 2026 |title='Bling Empire's Dorothy Wang Launching Wedding Series On YouTube |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/bling-empire-dorothy-wang-wedding-series-youtube-1237076119/ |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 2023, Wang moved to [[New York City]], having previously lived in Los Angeles.<ref name=":3" />

In October 2024, Wang announced her engagement to lawyer Brandon Yankowitz.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clack |first=Erin |date=October 29, 2024 |title=Bling Empire and Rich Kids of Beverly Hills Star Dorothy Wang Is Engaged to Lawyer Brandon Yankowitz |url=https://people.com/bling-empire-star-dorothy-wang-engaged-brandon-yankowitz-8736173 |website=[[People (magazine)|People]]}}</ref> The couple married exactly one year later on October 11, 2025, at Collegio alla Querce in [[Florence, Italy|Florence]], [[Italy]], with the reception at the [[Palazzo Corsini (Via del Parione)|Palazzo Corsini]]. The wedding was covered by ''[[Elle (magazine)|Elle]]'' and featured a performance by [[Saweetie]]. Her pre-wedding dress was custom designed by [[Prabal Gurung]], while her [[faille]] custom [[Oscar de la Renta]] wedding gown was designed by the label's co-creative directors [[Laura Kim]] and Fernando Garcia, the duos final wedding design before departing the label.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hildreth |first=Alexandra |date=October 28, 2025 |title=Dorothy Wang's Florence Wedding Featured Custom Oscar de la Renta and a Saweetie Surprise |url=https://www.elle.com/elleextra/events/a69148784/dorothy-wang-brandon-yankowitz-wedding-2025/ |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[Elle (magazine)|ELLE]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

On October 1, 2026, Wang announced she and Yankowitz were expecting their first child.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grant |first=Kayla |date=October 1, 2026 |title=Bling Empire's Dorothy Wang Is Pregnant, Expecting First Baby with Husband Brandon Yankowitz |url=https://people.com/dorothy-wang-expecting-her-first-baby-with-husband-brandon-yankowitz-12151776 |access-date=October 3, 2026 |website=[[People (magazine)|People]]}}</ref>

(Women)|Crystal Palace]] | caps15 = 20 | goals15 = 4 | years16 = 2025–2026 | clubs16 = [[Gotham FC]] | caps16 = 22 | goals16 = 1 | nationalyears1 = | nationalteam1 = [[United States women's national under-18 soccer team|United States U-18]] | nationalcaps1 = | nationalgoals1 = | nationalyears2 = 2011–2012 | nationalteam2 = [[United States women's national under-20 soccer team|United States U-20]] | nationalcaps2 = 19 | nationalgoals2 = 6 | nationalyears3 = 2014–2015 | nationalteam3 = [[United States women's national under-23 soccer team|United States U-23]] | nationalcaps3 = 6 | nationalgoals3 = 1 | club-update = 14:26, June 30, 2026 (UTC) | ntupdate = | totalcaps = 250+ | totalgoals = 70+ }} '''Katherine Nicole Lampson''' ({{née|'''Stengel'''}}; born February 29, 1992) is an American former professional [[women's association football|soccer]] player who played as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. Lampson previously played for the [[Boston Breakers]], [[Washington Spirit]], [[Utah Royals]], [[Houston Dash]], and [[NJ/NY Gotham FC|Gotham FC]] in the [[National Women's Soccer League]] (NWSL), [[FC Bayern Munich (women)|Bayern Munich]] in the German [[Frauen-Bundesliga]], both [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC (A-League Women)|Western Sydney Wanderers]] and [[Newcastle Jets FC (A-League Women)|Newcastle Jets]] in the Australian [[W-League (Australia)|W-League]], and both [[Liverpool F.C. Women|Liverpool]] and [[Crystal Palace F.C. (women)|Crystal Palace]] in the English [[Women's Super League]]. In 2012, she was part of the [[United States women's national under-20 soccer team|United States Under-20]] team that won the [[2012 CONCACAF Women's U-20 Championship]] and the [[2012 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup]]. ==Early life== Lampson attended [[Viera High School]] in [[Viera, Florida]].{{cite web |title=Katie Stengel Three-Time Soccer All-American |url=https://spacecoastdaily.com/2014/06/vieras-katie-stengel-three-time-soccer-all-american/ |website=Space Coast Daily |date=June 16, 2014 |access-date=August 7, 2020}} She attended [[Wake Forest University]] from 2010 to 2013 where she played for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons women's soccer|Demon Deacons women's soccer team]]. Lampson completed her college career as the highest-scoring player in Wake Forest history with 50 goals in 75 games, and she was a four-time All-ACC honoree and a three-time All-America, becoming in 2011 the first Wake Forest player to be named first-team All America. ==Club career== ===Bayern Munich=== In January 2014, Lampson skipped the [[2014 NWSL College Draft]] and instead joined the [[Los Angeles Blues]] of the since-disbanded [[USL W-League (1995–2015)|USL W-League]]. In June 2014, Lampson joined [[Frauen-Bundesliga]] side [[FC Bayern Munich (women)|Bayern Munich]].Includes [[Template League Cup]], [[Sample League Cup]] She helped Bayern win the 2014–15 Frauen Bundesliga title, leading the team with nine goals.{{cite news |last1=Kennedy |first1=Paul |title=Americans help Bayern win Frauen-Bundesliga title |url=http://www.socceramerica.com/article/63707/americans-help-bayern-win-frauen-bundesliga-title.html |access-date=July 27, 2015 |work=Soccer America |date=May 12, 2015}} ===Washington Spirit=== In December 2015, Lampson signed with the [[Washington Spirit]].{{cite news |last1=Kassouf |first1=Jeff |title=Spirit sign ex-Bayern Munich forward Katie Stengel |url=http://equalizersoccer.com/2015/12/30/washington-spirit-sign-katie-stengel-nwsl-bayern-munich/ |access-date=January 26, 2016 |work=Equalizer Soccer |date=December 30, 2015}} In her first season with the team, she played in 19 regular season matches, starting 10, totaling 928 minutes. Lampson contributed four goals during the season, tied for second most on the team.One appearance in Template Super Cup; two appearances, one goal in [[Template Centenary Cup]] In 2016 Washington advanced to the [[2016 National Women's Soccer League season|NWSL Championship Game]]. The game was tied 2–2 after extra time and went to penalties. Lampson converted her penalty, but Washington lost to the [[Western New York Flash]] 3–2 on penalties.{{cite web |url=https://us.soccerway.com/matches/2016/10/09/united-states/national-womens-soccer-league/washington-spirit/buffalo-flash/2362506/ |title=WASHINGTON SPIRIT VS. WESTERN NEW YORK FLASH 2 – 2 |access-date=November 23, 2018}} Lampson appeared in five games for the Spirit in [[2017 National Women's Soccer League season|2017]] before she was released by the club on June 28, 2017.{{Cite web |url=http://equalizersoccer.com/2017/06/28/wednesday-roundup-spirit-waive-castleberry-and-stengel/ |title=Wednesday Roundup: Spirit waive Castleberry and Stengel |publisher=The Equalizer |website=equalizersoccer.com |date=June 28, 2017 |access-date=June 29, 2017}}[[File:Katie Stengel.jpg|thumb|left|Katie Lampson playing for the Boston Breakers in the 2017 NWSL season]] ==== Western Sydney Wanderers (loan) ==== Lampson was signed by Australian team [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC (A-League Women)|Western Sydney Wanderers]] ahead of the [[2016–17 W-League]] season. She was the leading goal-scorer for the Wanderers, netting six goals for the season.{{Cite news |url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/newslocal/penrith-press/sport/quartet-of-us-footballers-lend-their-experience-to-wleague/news-story/3a7b74ca930189212f0466818b4f52eb |title=Quartet of US footballers lend their experience to W-League |last=Jones |first=Matt |date=November 18, 2016 |work=Daily Telegraph |access-date=June 23, 2017 |publisher=News Corp Australia |location=Sydney}}{{Cite news |url=http://westernweekender.com.au/2017/04/santa-named-wanderers-best/ |title=Santa named Wanderers' best |date=April 18, 2017 |work=The Western Weekender |access-date=June 23, 2017 |publisher=Western Sydney Publishing Group}} ===Boston Breakers=== The day after her release by the [[Washington Spirit]], Lampson was selected off waivers by the [[Boston Breakers]]. She appeared in 12 games for the Breakers in 2017.{{Cite web |url=http://www.bostonbreakerssoccer.com/common/mobile/mobile.html?jobid=73704&nogames=Y#a936062/ |title=Breakers claim Katie Stengel off of waivers |publisher=Boston Breakers |website=bostonbreakerssoccer.com |date=June 30, 2017 |access-date=June 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170623142923/http://www.bostonbreakerssoccer.com/common/mobile/mobile.html?jobid=73704&nogames=Y#a936062/ |archive-date=June 23, 2017 |url-status=dead}} ==== Newcastle Jets (loan) ==== In October 2017, Lampson returned to Australia, joining [[Newcastle Jets FC (A-League Women)|Newcastle Jets]] for the [[2017–18 W-League]] season.{{cite news |url=https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/4994215/newcastle-jets-lose-matildas-star-but-gain-us-striker-for-w-league-season/ |title=W-League: Newcastle Jets lose Matildas star but sign American striker |first=Craig |last=Kerry |newspaper=[[The Newcastle Herald]] |date=October 17, 2017 |access-date=October 20, 2017 |archive-date=October 17, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017150259/http://www.theherald.com.au/story/4994215/newcastle-jets-lose-matildas-star-but-gain-us-striker-for-w-league-season/ |url-status=live}} Lampson scored 10 goals for the Jets and finished second in the Golden Boot race behind [[Sam Kerr]]. Newcastle finished in third place and returned to the Finals series for the first time since the [[2008–09 W-League|2008–09]] season. Lampson returned to Newcastle for the [[2018–19 W-League]] season.{{cite web |url=https://www.w-league.com.au/news/w-league-stengel-locked-201819 |title=Stengel's back: Jets lock-in American striker for Westfield W-League 2018/19 Season |access-date=November 23, 2018 |date=October 3, 2018 |archive-date=October 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181009013327/https://www.w-league.com.au/news/w-league-stengel-locked-201819 |url-status=dead }} ===Utah Royals=== After the [[Boston Breakers]] folded ahead of the 2018 season, Lampson was selected by the [[Utah Royals]] in the Boston Breakers dispersal draft.{{Cite web |url=https://www.thebentmusket.com/2018/1/30/16949204/boston-breakers-players-nwsl-dispersal-draft |title=Boston Breakers players taken in NWSL dispersal draft |access-date=July 1, 2018 |date=January 30, 2018 |archive-date=September 10, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200910154404/https://www.thebentmusket.com/2018/1/30/16949204/boston-breakers-players-nwsl-dispersal-draft |url-status=dead }} Lampson appeared in 23 games for the Royals. She scored a team leading six goals and scored the first brace in Royals history.{{cite web |url=https://us.soccerway.com/players/katherine-nicole-stengel/229186/ |title=K.Stengel |access-date=November 23, 2018}} Lampson returned to the Royals for the [[2019 National Women's Soccer League season|2019 season]]. She appeared in all 24 games and scored 2 goals. ===Houston Dash=== On January 8, 2020, the Utah Royals traded Lampson and a third-round pick in the [[2020 NWSL College Draft]] to the [[Houston Dash]] in exchange for their second-round picks in the 2020 and 2021 College Drafts.{{cite web |url=https://www.rsl.com/post/2020/01/08/utah-royals-fc-receives-two-draft-picks-trade-houston-dash |title=UTAH ROYALS FC RECEIVES TWO DRAFT PICKS IN TRADE WITH THE HOUSTON DASH |access-date=January 8, 2020 |date=January 8, 2020}} She was waived by the club in May 2021.{{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/ksteng12/status/1395776990494531589 |title=Stengel waived |access-date=May 21, 2021}} ===Liverpool=== On January 6, 2022, Liverpool signed Lampson, reuniting her with manager [[Matt Beard]]. Lampson had played for Beard previously at the Boston Breakers.{{cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-fc-women-complete-signing-forward-katie-stengel |title=Liverpool FC Women complete signing of forward Katie Stengel |date=January 2022 |access-date=January 6, 2022}} ===NJ/NY Gotham FC=== [[File: Katie Lampson Gotham NC Courage Mar 21 2026-109.jpg|thumb|upright|Lampson with [[Gotham FC]] in 2026]] On July 5, 2023, Liverpool loaned Lampson to American club [[NJ/NY Gotham FC]] until September 3, 2023.{{cite press release |url=https://www.gothamfc.com/news_article/show/1278427 |title=Gotham FC Signs Katie Stengel on Loan from Liverpool |date=July 5, 2023 |access-date=July 5, 2023 |publisher=[[NJ/NY Gotham FC]] |archive-date=July 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705202215/https://www.gothamfc.com/news_article/show/1278427 |url-status=dead }} The loan was later made permanent, as Gotham acquired Lampson on a permanent transfer on September 13, 2023.{{Cite news |title=Liverpool striker Stengel joins US club Gotham FC |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66803721 |access-date=October 1, 2023}} ===Crystal Palace=== After just over a year at Gotham FC, Lampson signed a two-year deal with [[Crystal Palace F.C. (Women)|Crystal Palace]] on September 13, 2024.{{cite web |title=Crystal Palace Women Sign Katie Stengel |url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/announcement/crystal-palace-women-sign-katie-stengel/ |publisher=[[Crystal Palace F.C. (Women)|Crystal Palace]] |access-date=September 13, 2024 |date=September 13, 2024}}{{cite web |title=Crystal Palace sign NJ/NY Gotham FC forward Stengel |date=September 13, 2024 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/crystal-palace-sign-nj-ny-194400762.html}} === Gotham FC === Lampson returned to [[Gotham FC]] on July 31, 2025, with Crystal Palace relinquishing her in exchange for an undisclosed fee.{{Cite web |title=NWSL Champ Katie Stengel Returns to Gotham FC |url=https://www.gothamfc.com/news/nwsl-champ-katie-stengel-returns-to-gotham-fc |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=[[Gotham FC]] |language=en}} On February 24, 2026, it was announced that she had signed a contract extension with Gotham to keep her at the club through the [[2026 National Women's Soccer League season|2026 season]].{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2026 |title=Gotham FC's Katie Stengel Signs Contract Extension |url=https://www.gothamfc.com/news/gotham-fcs-katie-stengel-signs-contract-extension |access-date=February 24, 2026 |website=Gotham FC |language=en}} On June 30, 2026, Lampson announced her retirement from professional soccer.{{Cite web |title=Two-Time NWSL Champion Katie Lampson Announces Retirement from Professional Soccer |url=https://www.gothamfc.com/news/twotime-nwsl-champion-katie-lampson-announces-retirement-from-professional-soccer |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=Gotham FC |language=en}} == International career == With the [[United States women's national under-20 soccer team|United States Under-20]] team Lampson won the [[2012 CONCACAF Women's U-20 Championship]]. At the [[2012 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup]], Lampson appeared in four games and scored three goals. The United States won the U-20 World Cup. Lampson has also played for the [[United States women's national under-23 soccer team|United States U-23 women's national team]]. In March 2014, she received her first [[United States women's national soccer team|full national team]] call-up from head coach [[Tom Sermanni]]. Lampson has not yet been capped by the USWNT.{{cite news |last1=Dowling |first1=Lyn |title=Viera's Stengel named to U.S. Women's National Team |url=http://www.floridatoday.com/story/sports/2014/03/27/vieras-stengel-named-uswnt/6977839/ |access-date=July 27, 2015 |work=Florida Today |date=March 28, 2014}} == Personal life== Lampson's younger sister Jackie played for [[NC State Wolfpack|North Carolina State University]] and her father Scott played for the [[Air Force Falcons men's soccer|Air Force Academy]].{{cite news |last1=Hays |first1=Graham |title=Stengel Sisters Making Their Own Names |url=https://www.espn.com/espnw/news-commentary/story/_/id/9681278/espnw-jackie-katie-stengel-making-their-own-names-college-soccer |access-date=July 27, 2015 |work=espnW |date=September 18, 2013}} She announced her engagement to former professional goalkeeper [[Matt Lampson]] in January 2026. They married around a month later, and she subsequently began using her married name professionally.{{cite press release |title=Gotham FC Announces Leadership Group, Roster Ahead of 2026 Season |url=https://www.gothamfc.com/news/gotham-fc-announces-leadership-group-roster-ahead-of-2026-season |work=Gotham FC |date=March 5, 2026}} == Career statistics == === Club === {{updated|match played September 13, 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/-/229186/ |title=USA – K. '''David Castañeda Jr.''' (born October 24, 1989) is an American actor. In 2019, Castañeda began portraying [[Number Two / The Kraken (Diego Hargreeves)|Diego Hargreeves]] in the [[Netflix]] series ''[[The Umbrella Academy (TV series)|The Umbrella Academy]]''.

==Early life==
Castañeda was born October 24, 1989,<ref name=popbuzz>{{Cite web|url=https://www.popbuzz.com/tv-film/features/david-castaneda/|title=David Castañeda: 11 facts about the ''Umbrella Academy'' star you probably didn't know|website=PopBuzz|access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref> in [[Los Angeles]]<ref name="chicago tribune">{{cite web |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sns-bc-esp-tel-umbrella-academy-david-castaeda-20190223-story.html |title=David Castañeda: 'Los pleitos de hermanos son saludables'marry my |first=Berenice |last=Bautista |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=February 23, 2019 |access-date=February 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190226173305/https://www.chicagotribune.com/sns-bc-esp-tel-umbrella-academy-david-castaeda-20190223-story.html |archive-date=February 26, 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and was raised in [[Sinaloa]], Mexico.<ref name="golden globes"/>{{efn|One source says he is a native of [[Sinaloa]], Mexico and moved to the US at age 14.<ref name="golden globes"/> Another source says he was born in Los Angeles, raised in Mexico, then went to the US for high school.<ref name="chicago tribune" />}} He returned to the United States when he was 4 and attended [[Workman High School|William Workman High School]] in California.<ref name="chicago tribune" /> Castañeda initially studied [[civil engineering]] in college with the intention of taking over the family business after he finished his studies.<ref name=status /> However, he became interested in film direction and switched to major in film production and international business in 2007 at [[California State University, Fullerton]].<ref name="golden globes">{{cite web |url=https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/david-castaneda-el-morro-de-burgermania-anda-de-actor-en-hollywood |title=David Castañeda: 'El morro de Burgermanía anda de actor en Hollywood' |first=Gabriel |last=Lerman |date=February 15, 2019 |publisher=[[Golden Globes]] |access-date=February 28, 2019 |language=Spanish |archive-date=January 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109071302/https://www.goldenglobes.com/articles/david-castaneda-el-morro-de-burgermania-anda-de-actor-en-hollywood |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=titan>{{cite web |url=https://dailytitan.com/2013/11/student-balances-acting-with-responsibilities-on-switched-at-birth-tv-series/ |title=Student balances acting with responsibilities on ''Switched at Birth'' TV series |first=Sonam |last= Mirpuri |date=November 5, 2013 |work=Daily Titan|access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref> Castañeda then moved into acting and started auditioning for roles. He studied part-time while pursuing an acting career, eventually graduating in 2015.<ref name=titan /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/2xAZXRm4VY/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/instagram/castanedawong/986571536349234520 |archive-date=2021-12-25 |url-access=registration|title=Assemble |author=castanedawong|website=[[Instagram]] |date=May 17, 2015 |access-date=February 28, 2019}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

==Career==
Castañeda has been involved in acting since he was 17,<ref name=status>{{cite web |url=http://statusmagonline.com/features/davidcastaneda-interview-february2019/ |title=David Castañeda Steers His Plans To An Action-Packed Acting Career |first=Nikki |last=Yap |date=February 2019 |work=Status |via=statusmagonline.com |access-date=February 28, 2019 |archive-date=February 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190218195906/http://statusmagonline.com/features/davidcastaneda-interview-february2019/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> but only started taking acting more seriously after he volunteered for a role when a director asked for actors to participate in his film during a seminar while at university.<ref name=titan /> He played various minor roles in a number of productions, such as ''[[End of Watch]]'', and also acted as a main character in a short film ''Maddoggin{{'}}'', which won the audience award at the NBC Universal Short Cut Film Festival.<ref name=titan /> In 2013, he landed a role playing Jorge on [[Freeform (TV channel)|ABC Family]]'s TV series ''[[Switched at Birth (TV series)|Switched at Birth]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/melissa-joey-switched-at-birth-650299 |title=''Melissa & Joey'', ''Switched at Birth'' Add Guest Stars |date=October 23, 2013 |first= Philiana |last=Ng |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=February 28, 2019 }}</ref> In late 2016, he was cast in the role of Hector in the film ''[[Sicario: Day of the Soldado]]'' released in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://variety.com/2016/film/news/david-castaneda-sicario-sequel-soldado-1201943575/ |title= David Castaneda Joins ''Sicario'' Sequel ''Soldado''|first= Justin |last= Kroll |work=Variety |date=December 15, 2016|access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref>  He also has a major role in an independent film ''[[El Chicano (film)|El Chicano]]'', a supporting role in [[Jean-Claude Van Damme]]'s ''We Die Young'' as well as minor roles in films such as the [[Billy Crystal]]'s film ''[[Standing Up, Falling Down]]''.<ref name=status />

In 2017, he was cast in his most prominent role yet playing [[Number Two / The Kraken (Diego Hargreeves)|Diego Hargreeves / Number 2]] in ''[[The Umbrella Academy (TV series)|The Umbrella Academy]]'',<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://variety.com/2017/tv/news/umbrella-academy-series-netflix-cast-1202627134/|title=''Umbrella Academy'' Netflix Series Rounds Out Cast With ''Game of Thrones'' Alum, ''Hamilton'' Star|last=Otterson|first=Joe|date=November 30, 2017|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=November 30, 2017}}</ref> which was released on [[Netflix]] in February 2019, the first of a four season run.

{{Nihongo|'''Shunsuke Takeuchi'''|武内 駿輔|Takeuchi Shunsuke|born September 12, 1997}} is a [[Voice acting in Japan|Japanese voice actor]], singer, and music producer affiliated with [[81 Produce]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.81produce.co.jp/list.cgi?man+3114033222730|script-title=ja:武内駿輔：所属俳優|website=[[81 Produce]]|access-date=January 14, 2017|archive-date=April 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170417125358/http://www.81produce.co.jp/list.cgi?man+3114033222730|url-status=dead}}</ref> He won the award for Best Rookie Actor at the [[10th Seiyu Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2016-03-12/yoshitsugu-matsuoka-inori-minase-win-10th-annual-seiyu-awards/.99694|title=Yoshitsugu Matsuoka, Inori Minase Win 10th Annual Seiyū Awards (Updated)|date=March 12, 2016|accessdate=March 12, 2016|work=[[Anime News Network]]|archive-date=May 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170505123819/http://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2016-03-12/yoshitsugu-matsuoka-inori-minase-win-10th-annual-seiyu-awards/.99694|url-status=live}}</ref> His roles include Producer in ''[[The Idolmaster Cinderella Girls]]'', Alexander Yamato in ''[[King of Prism]]'', [[Einar (Vinland Saga)|Einar]] in ''[[Vinland Saga (manga)|Vinland Saga]]'', [[List of Bleach characters #D: Askin Nakk Le Vaar|Askin Nakk Le Vaar]] in ''[[Bleach (manga)|Bleach]]'', Zodyl in ''[[Gachiakuta]]'', Juza Hyodo in ''[[A3!]]'', Revolver in ''[[Yu-Gi-Oh! VRAINS]]'', Zack Walker in ''[[Astra Lost in Space]]'', and Brawler in ''[[Akudama Drive]]''.

Takeuchi is part of the musical duo Amadeus with rapper Lotus Juice as the vocalist and music producer, performing under the stage name '''Jack Westwood'''.<ref>{{cite news | first=Taizo | last=Nishio | url=https://nlab.itmedia.co.jp/nl/articles/1804/02/news096.html | script-title=ja:武内駿輔「左手薬指の指輪は魔除け」発言、「ファン {{=}} 魔物」派を召喚してしまう | language=ja | work=Netlab | via=ITmedia | date=April 2, 2018 | accessdate=May 27, 2021 | archive-date=March 13, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220313171542/https://nlab.itmedia.co.jp/nl/articles/1804/02/news096.html | url-status=live }}</ref> He is also credited under the name for his music productions.

He currently drives the No. 18 [[Chevrolet Camaro ZL1]] for [[Team 18]] in the [[Supercars Championship|Repco Supercars Championship]]. He briefly raced in various [[Formula Renault]] series in [[Europe]] and the [[Dunlop Super2 Series]]. ==Career== [[File:Holden Commodore ZB of Anton de Pasquale (2018 Adelaide 500).jpg|thumb|The [[Holden Commodore ZB]] of Anton de Pasquale at the [[2018 Adelaide 500]]]] ===Karting=== De Pasquale competed in the Australian National Sprint Kart Championship from 2010 to 2011, winning the championship in 2011.{{cite news | url=https://www.karting.net.au/karting-australia/champions | title=Australian Kart Champions | work=Karting Australia | accessdate=21 January 2025}} ===Formula Ford=== De Pasquale raced in the Victorian Formula Ford Championship, taking second place in the championship. He then moved to the Australian Formula Ford Championship, where he raced for two seasons, eventually winning the championship in 2013.{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/anton-de-pasquale-storms-double-pole-position/ | title=Anton De Pasquale storms to double pole position | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=20 April 2014}} ===Formula Renault=== De Pasquale then moved to Europe to compete in the [[2014 Formula Renault seasons#2014 Formula Renault 1.6 NEC season|Formula Renault 1.6 NEC Championship]], winning seven races and gaining three podiums and winning the championship.{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/de-pasquale-precipice-title-glory/ | title=De Pasquale on precipice of title glory | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=7 October 2014}}{{cite news| url=https://speedcafe.com/de-pasquale-ready-formula-renault-1-6-debut/ | title=De Pasquale ready for Formula Renault 1.6 debut | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=18 April 2014}} De Pasquale then shifted to the [[2015 Eurocup Formula Renault 2.0|Eurocup Formula Renault 2.0]] racing for [[Koiranen GP]] for all but five races. He scored four points and ended the season in 18th place.{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/world-wrap-btcc-title-race-wide-open/ | title=WORLD WRAP: BTCC title race wide open | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=7 September 2015}}{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/de-pasquale-secures-top-formula-renault-drive/ | title=De Pasquale secures top Formula Renault drive | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=21 December 2014}} ===Supercars Dunlop Series=== De Pasquale then moved back into Australia to compete in the [[2016 Supercars Dunlop Series]] racing for [[Paul Morris Motorsport]].{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/open-wheel-convert-taps-v8-experience/ | title=Open-wheel convert taps into V8 experience | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=17 February 2016}} He scored one podium and finished in eleventh place in the standings. In [[2017 Super2 Series|2017]], he finished fourth.{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/hazelwood-wins-super2-title-dramatic-newcastle-finale/ | title=Hazelwood wins Super2 title in dramatic finale | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=26 November 2017}} ===Erebus Motorsport=== For the [[2018 Supercars Championship]], de Pasquale moved to [[Erebus Motorsport]] on a multi year deal.{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/erebus-signs-anton-de-pasquale-2018/ | title=Erebus signs Anton De Pasquale for 2018 | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=31 October 2017}} He had his first win at [[Hidden Valley Raceway]] in [[2020 Supercars Championship|2020]].{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/de-pasquale-finessing-set-up-key-to-repeat-darwin-results/ | title=De Pasquale: Finessing set-up key to repeat Darwin results | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=20 August 2020}} ===Dick Johnson Racing=== De Pasquale moved to [[Dick Johnson Racing|DJR Team Penske]] in 2021 for four years,{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/story-djr-can-win-without-mclaughlin/ | title=De Pasquale: Finessing set-up key to repeat Darwin results | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=20 August 2020}} taking eight wins. ===Team 18=== For the [[2025 Supercars Championship]], De Pasquale moved to [[Team 18]].{{cite news | url=https://speedcafe.com/supercars-news-paul-morris-anton-de-pasquale-djr-split/ | title=Story: DJR can win without McLaughlin | work=[[Speedcafe]] | date=20 January 2021}} De Pasquale finished 8th in the championship in his first season with the team, achieving three podiums. De Pasquale began his second season with Team 18 with the team taking on the role as the [[Chevrolet]] homologation team. De Pasquale started the season strongly at the first round of the Championship, the [[Sydney Motorsport Park Supercars round|Sydney 500]], claiming pole position for race 2 and converting it into the race victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.supercars.com/news/supercars-news-2026-race-2-top-10-shootout-report-sydney-anton-de-pasquale-pole-position-team-18-chevrolet|title=Rain smiles on De Pasquale to claim shock Shootout pole|publisher=[[Supercars Championship]]|date=21 February 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://speedcafe.com/supercars-news-2026-sydney-500-saturday-race-2-results-anton-de-pasquale-wins-podium-reaction-highlights-video/|title=De Pasquale denies Kostecki in Sydney 500 thriller|publisher=[[Speedcafe]]|date=21 February 2026}} It was both his first pole position and race win for Team 18. Over the following rounds, De Pasquale established himself as the lead Chevrolet driver in the championship,{{cite web|url=https://www.supercars.com/news/supercars-news-2026-anton-de-pasquale-team-18-real-deal-charlie-schwerkolt-chevrolet-general-motors-sydney|title=Schwerkolt: De Pasquale the 'No. 1 Chev driver', Team 18 the 'real deal'|publisher=[[Supercars Championship]]|date=26 February 2026}} and picked up his second win of the season at Hidden Valley, in race 19 of the championship.{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/v8supercars/news/supercars-darwin-anton-de-pasquale-takes-commanding-hidden-valley-victory/10832088/|title=Supercars Darwin: Anton De Pasquale takes commanding Hidden Valley victory|publisher=[[Motorsport.com]]|date=21 June 2026}} This victory was the first of four podium finishes in seven races, followed by driving from eleventh on the grid to finish second at the [[Townsville 500]],{{cite web|url=https://speedcafe.com/supercars-news-2026-townsville-500-race-2-results-saturday-matt-payne-wins-anton-de-pasquale-stars-reaction-comments-highlights/|title=Payne scores Saturday Townsville win as De Pasquale stars|publisher=[[Speedcafe]]|date=11 July 2026}} and then twice finishing third at the [[Wanneroo Supercars round|Perth Super 440]].{{cite web|url=https://au.motorsport.com/v8supercars/news/supercars-perth-matt-payne-outduels-broc-feeney-for-victory/10843666/|title=Supercars Perth: Matt Payne outduels Broc Feeney for victory|publisher=[[Motorsport.com]]|date=2 August 2026}} ==Career results== === Karting career summary === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size: 85%; text-align:center" !Season !Series !Position |- !rowspan=14| 2010 | align="left" |Australian National Sprint Kart Championship - '''Valentín Perales''' (born 2 August 1995) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for Chilean club [[Unión San Felipe]].<ref name="Soccerway">{{cite news|title=Argentina - V. Perales|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/valentin-perales/248503/|accessdate=19 December 2018|work=Soccerway}}</ref>

==Career==
Perales began in [[Club Cipolletti|Cipolletti]]'s ranks, the defender featured eighteen times in the [[2012–13 Torneo Argentino A]]; his debut came on 26 August 2012 against [[Defensores de Belgrano de Villa Ramallo|Defensores de Belgrano]], while he also scored his first goal in a game with [[Club y Biblioteca Ramón Santamarina|Santamarina]] on 25 November.<ref name="Soccerway"/><ref name="BDFA">{{cite news|title=Ficha Estadistica de VALENTIN PERALES|url=https://www.bdfa.com.ar/jugadores-VALENTIN-PERALES-89742.html|accessdate=19 December 2018|work=BDFA}}</ref> At the end of 2012–13, Perales was signed by [[Argentine Primera División]] side [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]].<ref name="Soccerway"/><ref name="Olé">{{cite news|title=No conozco Buenos Aires|url=https://www.ole.com.ar/san-lorenzo/conozco-buenos-aires_0_BkXlquNyo2l.html|accessdate=19 December 2018|work=Olé|date=4 February 2013}}</ref> In February 2015, after no appearances, Perales rejoined Cipolletti on loan.<ref name="Soccerway"/> One goal in thirty-two games followed.<ref name="Soccerway"/> On 7 July 2016, Perales joined [[Deportivo Morón]] of [[Primera B Metropolitana]].<ref name="Soccerway"/> He scored in their final match of their promotion-winning season of [[2016–17 Primera B Metropolitana|2016–17]] versus [[Deportivo Riestra]].<ref name="Soccerway"/><ref name="Copa Argentina">{{cite news|title=Perales quiere que su destino vuelva a cruzarse con Cipolletti o San Lorenzo|url=https://www.copaargentina.org/es/noticias/6933_Perales-quiere-que-su-destino-vuelva-a-cruzarse-con-Cipolletti-o-San-Lorenzo.html|accessdate=19 December 2018|work=Copa Argentina|date=31 May 2017}}</ref>

In December 2025, Perales moved to Chile and signed with [[Unión San Felipe]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Nuevo fichaje de Unión San Felipe: zaguero argentino refuerza al Uní-Uní |url=https://primerabchile.cl/valentin-perales-nuevo-fichaje-de-union-san-felipe/ |access-date=28 December 2025 |work=PrimeraBChile.cl |date=26 December 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

Aoyama debuted as a gravure idol in 2013.<ref name="mynavi160515" /> In April of the same year, she won the first "Jigadoru" Contest Grand Prix ([[Lily Franky]] Award) and in October, won the Nippon TV's "Shiodome Gravure Koshien 2014" Special Fan Award. She also won the Idol DVD Award as Selected by Professionals 2014.

In May 2015, she graduated from her gravure idol group of ''Sakuragaoka Chocolat'' and joined a new group called ''Sherbet'' in August of the same year.

In a 2016 collaboration, Aoyama modeled for the fashion brand [[Kiks Tyo]] on a series of six limited edition "Kiks Girls" photo t-shirts.<ref>{{cite web |title=NEW KIKS GIRLS TEE |url=https://twitter.com/kikstyo/status/811855775840681984?lang=gl |website=Twitter |access-date=15 July 2023 |date=Dec 22, 2016}}</ref>

She left her former agency, ''Entermax Promotions'', in 2017 and joined her current agency, ''01familia''. She continues her activities with appearances on magazine covers, often with other models of her agency.<ref>{{Cite news|title=増刊ヤングジャンプGOLD Vol.4｜Weekly Young Jump Official Site|last=[[Weekly Young Jump]]｜[[Shueisha]]|url=https://youngjump.jp/yjgold/|accessdate=2019-04-29|language=ja-JP|work=Weekly Young Jump Official Site}}</ref> She was the lead actress in the ''[[Miss Machiko]]'' stage play adaptation.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Miss Machiko Stage Play Revealed With Visual |url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2017-07-10/miss-machiko-stage-play-revealed-with-visual/.118630|work=[[Anime News Network]]|language=en|date=2017-07-10}}</ref>

She made an appearance in the video game ''[[Yakuza Kiwami 2]]'' as a gravure idol, which was released in December 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dengekionline.com/elem/000/001/598/1598624/|title=『龍が如く 極2』でグラビア撮影を体験できる。堂島の龍もご満悦！【TGS2017】|accessdate=2019-04-29|date=2017-09-24|publisher=Dengeki Online}}</ref>

'''Julia Margareta Zigiotti Olme''' (born 24 December 1997) is a Swedish professional [[footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for [[Women's Super League]] club [[Manchester United W.F.C.|Manchester United]] and the [[Sweden women's national football team|Sweden national team]]. 

==Club career==

=== Early career ===
Zigiotti joined the youth ranks of [[Bollstanäs SK]] in her home locality of [[Upplands Väsby]], making her senior debut in her mid-teens. Between 2014 and 2018, she played with [[AIK Fotboll (women)|AIK]] and [[Hammarby Fotboll (women)|Hammarby]] in Sweden's [[Damallsvenskan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julia Zigiotti - Women's Team {{!}} Manchester United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/teams/womens-team/julia-zigiotti-olme |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=Manchester United |language=en}}</ref>

=== BK Häcken ===
Zigiotti joined [[Kopparbergs/Göteborg FC]] from [[Hammarby Fotboll (women)|Hammarby]] in 2018.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |title=Brighton sign Emma Kullberg & Julia Zigiotti Olme |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59840139 |access-date=1 January 2022 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=1 January 2022 |archive-date=24 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124053009/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59840139 |url-status=live }}</ref> In November 2020, Zigiotti Olme won the [[Damallsvenskan]] with Kopparbergs/Göteborg FC, the club's first league title.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 November 2020 |title=Spelare, tränare, ledare – här är guldgänget 2020- Kopparbergs Göteborg FC |url=https://www.goteborgfc.se/nyheter/spelare-traenare-ledare-haer-aer-guldgaenget-2020/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109213525/https://www.goteborgfc.se/nyheter/spelare-traenare-ledare-haer-aer-guldgaenget-2020/ |archive-date=9 November 2020 |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=Goteborg FC |language=sv}}</ref> Just days after the win, the club announced its plans to cease operations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 December 2020 |title=KGFC avbryter elitsatsningen- Kopparbergs Göteborg FC |url=https://www.goteborgfc.se/nyheter/kgfc-avbryter-elitsatsningen/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201229111414/https://www.goteborgfc.se/nyheter/kgfc-avbryter-elitsatsningen/ |archive-date=29 December 2020 |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=Goteborg FC |language=sv}}</ref> This decision was shortly reversed, but the club became part of [[BK Häcken]], operating under the name Bollklubben Häcken Fotbollsförening ([[BK Häcken FF]]).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Rory |date=24 February 2021 |title=In Women’s Soccer, a Rising Tide Sinks One Boat |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/24/sports/soccer/champions-league-womens-soccer.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409054004/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/24/sports/soccer/champions-league-womens-soccer.html |archive-date=9 April 2023 |access-date=14 June 2026 |work=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref> Zigiotti Olme underwent surgery on both hips in December 2020, and was sidelined for six months.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Jacobs |first=Ben |date=30 July 2024 |title=Exclusive: Julia Zigiotti Olme Joins Bayern Munich After Brighton Exit |url=https://www.givemesport.com/exclusive-julia-zigotti-olme-joins-bayern-munich-after-brighton-exit/ |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=GiveMeSport |language=en |archive-date=24 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250924231847/https://www.givemesport.com/exclusive-julia-zigotti-olme-joins-bayern-munich-after-brighton-exit/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In October 2021, Zigiotti was on the bench as Häcken missed out on a chance to win their second Damallsvenskan title; her agent alleged that she was excluded from the match because she had not signed a new contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rydén |first=Anna |last2=Karlsson |first2=Mattias |date=19 October 2021 |title=Julia Zigiotti Olme efter petningen: ”Stel stämning” |url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/V9jB3d |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=SPORTBLADET |language=sv}}</ref>

=== Brighton & Hove Albion ===
In January 2022, Zigiotti joined [[FA Women's Super League|Women's Super League]] club [[Brighton & Hove Albion W.F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] on an 18-month contract in a double transfer with international teammate (and partner) [[Emma Kullberg]].<ref name=":0" /> 

She was named Player's Player of the Season for her performance in the [[2022–23 Brighton & Hove Albion W.F.C. season|2022–23 campaign]].<ref name=":2">{{cite news |title=Julia Zigiotti signs new contract|url=https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/3622713/julia-zigiotti-signs-new-contract/ |access-date=9 August 2023 |publisher=Brighton & Hove Albion FC |date=9 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810060639/https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/news/3622713/julia-zigiotti-signs-new-contract|archive-date=10 August 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref> She captained the club during the latter part of the season before losing the armband under new head coach [[Melissa Phillips]].<ref name=":1" /> On 9 August 2023, she signed a new contract with Brighton.<ref name=":2" />

On 24 July 2024, it was announced that Zigiotti had left the club after the expiry of her contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=Julia Zigiotti Leaves Albion |url=https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/modals/en/media-article-popup/wft-news-transfer-news-julia-zigiotti-leaves-albion |access-date=24 July 2024 |publisher=Brighton & Hove Albion FC |date=24 July 2024 |archive-date=24 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240724145742/https://www.brightonandhovealbion.com/modals/en/media-article-popup/wft-news-transfer-news-julia-zigiotti-leaves-albion |url-status=live }}</ref> She had rejected a contract extension from Brighton.<ref name=":1" />

=== Bayern Munich ===
On 30 July 2024, Zigiotti signed a two-year contract with [[Frauen-Bundesliga]] side [[FC Bayern Munich (women)|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FC Bayern Women sign Julia Zigiotti Olme |url=https://fcbayern.com/frauen/en/news/2024/07/fc-bayern-women-sign-julia-zigiotti-olme |website=fcbayern.com |publisher=FC Bayern München |access-date=30 July 2024 |date=30 July 2024 |archive-date=24 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250224031707/https://fcbayern.com/frauen/en/news/2024/07/fc-bayern-women-sign-julia-zigiotti-olme |url-status=live }}</ref> With Bayern, she won the domestic treble: the Frauen-Bundesliga,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lamparter |first=Margot |date=27 April 2025 |title=Meisterschaft perfekt: FC Bayern Frauen feiern siebten Titel |url=https://www.br.de/nachrichten/sport/fussball-bundesliga-frauen-20-spieltag-fc-bayern-gegen-sc-freiburg,UjYvumZ |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=BR24 |language=de |archive-date=18 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260218012406/https://www.br.de/nachrichten/sport/fussball-bundesliga-frauen-20-spieltag-fc-bayern-gegen-sc-freiburg,UjYvumZ |url-status=live }}</ref> the [[DFB-Pokal Frauen|DFB-Pokal]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bayern München - Werder Bremen, 4:2, Women's DFB-Pokal 2024/25 final |url=https://datencenter.dfb.de/en/data-center/women-s-dfb-cup/2024-25/final/2394536 |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=DFB |language=en |archive-date=1 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250501172029/https://datencenter.dfb.de/en/data-center/women-s-dfb-cup/2024-25/final/2394536 |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[DFB-Supercup Frauen|DFB-Supercup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bayern München - VfL Wolfsburg, 1:0, Google Pixel Supercup 2024 final |url=https://datencenter.dfb.de/en/data-center/google-pixel-supercup/19032/final/2375436 |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=DFB |language=en}}</ref>

=== Manchester United ===
On 31 July 2025, Zigiotti signed for [[Manchester United W.F.C.|Manchester United]] in the [[Women's Super League|WSL]] on a two-year contract with the option for a further year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Coates |first1=Charlotte |title=Man Utd sign Sweden midfielder Zigiotti from Bayern |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c707eeg9dj0o |website=BBC Sport |access-date=31 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250731102816/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c707eeg9dj0o |archive-date=31 July 2025 |date=31 July 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> She made her club debut on 10 September, with head coach Marc Skinner describing her as "exceptional".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinoti |first=Derick |date=2025-09-10 |title=Marc Skinner hails early impact of "exceptional" signing Julia Zigiotti Olme |url=https://thepeoplesperson.com/2025/09/10/marc-skinner-hails-early-impact-of-exceptional-signing-julia-zigiotti-olme-298769/ |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=The Peoples Person |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 7 February 2026, she scored her first goal for the club in a 0–2 win over Leicester City; she also assisted [[Elisabeth Terland]]'s second-half goal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cowen |first=Ailsa |date=7 February 2026 |title=Leicester City 0-2 Manchester United: Julia Zigiotti Olme and Elisabeth Terland score for visitors |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cq6vnlmjjdqt |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=10 February 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260210142727/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cq6vnlmjjdqt |url-status=live }}</ref>

== International career ==
Zigiotti Olme was first called up to the senior [[Sweden women's national football team|Sweden national team]] in September 2018. 

In May 2019, she was called up to the Swedish team for the [[2019 FIFA Women's World Cup|2019 Women's World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.svenskfotboll.se/nyheter/landslag/2019/5/dam-vm-trupp/|title=Gerhardssons VM-trupp presenterad|trans-title=Gerhardsson's World Cup squad presented|language=Swedish|publisher=[[Swedish Football Association]]|date=16 May 2019|access-date=19 May 2019|archive-date=7 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607141934/https://www.svenskfotboll.se/nyheter/landslag/2019/5/dam-vm-trupp/|url-status=live}}</ref> Sweden beat [[England women's national football team|England]] to claim third-place at the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 July 2019 |title=Sweden down England to finish third |url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/national/fifa_womens_world_cup/news/sweden_down_england_to_finish_third.html |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=The AFC |language=en |archive-date=10 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250910165955/https://www.the-afc.com/en/national/fifa_womens_world_cup/news/sweden_down_england_to_finish_third.html |url-status=live }}</ref> She was not called up to team for the [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]], [[UEFA Women's Euro 2022|2022 Women's Euro]] or the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup|2023 Women's World Cup]]. 

Zigiotti represented Sweden at the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2025|2025 Women's Euro]] tournament in [[Switzerland]], where Sweden were eliminated in the quarter-finals through a 2–3 penalty shootout loss to eventual champions England. Only Zigiotti Olme and [[Nathalie Björn]] scored their penalties for Sweden, with Player of the Match [[Hannah Hampton]] making two saves and five Swedish players recording misses.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sweden vs England {{!}} UEFA Women's EURO 2025 |url=https://www.uefa.com/womenseuro/match/2044379--sweden-vs-england/ |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=UEFA |language=en |archive-date=6 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260606134902/https://www.uefa.com/womenseuro/match/2044379--sweden-vs-england/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Zigiotti born to a [[Italians|Italian]] mother and a Swedish father.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-11-28 |title=Julia Zigiotti Olme interview: Ziggy and the Swede Stardust – Melody maketh the medals for Sweden midfielder – Beats & Rhymes FC |url=https://beatsandrhymesfc.com/julia-zigiotti-olme-interview-ziggy-and-the-swede-stardust-melody-maketh-the-medals-for-sweden-midfielder/ |access-date=2025-07-12 |language=en-US |archive-date=12 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250912131932/https://beatsandrhymesfc.com/julia-zigiotti-olme-interview-ziggy-and-the-swede-stardust-melody-maketh-the-medals-for-sweden-midfielder/ |url-status=live }}</ref> She has always intended to play for Sweden internationally, and plays with her mother's surname to honour her Italian side.<ref name=":1" /> She was a childhood [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] supporter, and idolised [[Alessandro Del Piero]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nilsson |first1=Jonathan |date=21 September 2018 |title=Anfallstalangen om landslaget: "Kom som en chock" |publisher=[[Aftonbladet]] |url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/sportbladet/fotboll/a/wEGbwP/anfallstalangen-om-landslaget-kom-som-en-chock |access-date=19 May 2019 |archive-date=18 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190418193424/https://www.aftonbladet.se/sportbladet/fotboll/a/wEGbwP/anfallstalangen-om-landslaget-kom-som-en-chock |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Zigiotti was in a relationship with her [[BK Häcken FF|Häcken]] and [[Brighton & Hove Albion W.F.C.|Brighton]] teammate and fellow Swedish footballer [[Emma Kullberg]].<ref>[https://www.l-mag.de/news-1010/das-sind-die-50-lesbischen-stars-der-fussball-em-2022.html L-Mag.de: Das sind die 59 lesbischen Stars der Fussball-EM 2022 (German)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220721201419/https://www.l-mag.de/news-1010/das-sind-die-50-lesbischen-stars-der-fussball-em-2022.html |date=21 July 2022 }}, July 2022</ref> The pair became engaged in 2022, but appeared to have split by 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vendela |first=Ögren |last2=Olsson |first2=Frida |date=28 May 2025 |title=Landslagsspelarna bryter förlovningen: ”Inte så mycket att säga om det” |url=https://www.expressen.se/sport/fotboll/landslaget/julia-zigiotti-olme-och-emma-kullberg-bryter-forlovningen/ |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=Expressen |language=sv}}</ref>

'''Kirvil Odden Sundsfjord''' (born 29 July 1992) is a Norwegian [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Lyn Fotball Damer|Lyn]].

==Career==
Odden hails from [[Notodden Municipality]] and started her career in [[SK Snøgg]].<ref name=telen20/> Concurrently with her football career in the Third Division, she competed on national level in age-specific [[track and field]], mostly high jump, shot put and discus throw.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telen.no/sport/sport/kirvil-pa-landslaget/s/2-2.3402-1.4707444|title=Kirvil på landslaget|author=Vik, Glenn|work=Telen|date=25 February 2010|language=no|access-date=7 September 2023}}</ref> In her late teenages, she moved to [[Oslo]] and had spells in [[Røa IL]] and [[Kolbotn Fotball|Kolbotn IL]] before returning to Røa in 2014.<ref>{{NFF|2694253}}</ref> She became Røa's first choice in 2017 following the retirement of [[Silje Vesterbekkmo]]. Odden was selected as team [[captain (association football)|captain]] ahead of the 2018 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telen.no/kirvil-schau-odden/fotball/sport/na-har-kirvil-blitt-kaptein-pa-roa/s/5-75-166744|title=Nå har Kirvil blitt kaptein på Røa|author=Kaasa, Trond|date=17 April 2018|work=Telen|language=no|access-date=3 September 2023}}</ref>

However, after the 2019 season she had lost motivation to continue, and terminated her contract. She agreed to move to city rivals [[Lyn Fotball Damer|Lyn]].<ref name=telen20>{{cite news|url=https://www.telen.no/kirvil-matte-gjore-et-toft-valg-hun-matte-komme-seg-vekk-na-har-hun-slatt-kraftig-tilbake/f/5-75-452105|title= Kirvil måtte gjøre et tøft valg. Hun måtte komme seg vekk. Nå har hun slått kraftig tilbake|author=Kaasa, Trond|date=25 December 2020|work=Telen|language=no|access-date=3 September 2023}}</ref> She became club captain here as well, in 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telen.no/det-a-motta-denne-prisen-er-kanskje-noe-av-det-storste-jeg-har-opplevd/s/5-75-502686|title= – Det å motta denne prisen er kanskje noe av det største jeg har opplevd!|author=Kivle, Kristine|date=14 July 2021|work=Telen|language=no|access-date=3 September 2023}}</ref>

In 2022 Odden was contacted and signed by Italian club [[UC Sampdoria (women)|Sampdoria]].<ref name=italy>{{cite news|url=https://vartoslo.no/bydel-nordre-aker-bydel-sagene-frida-maanum/lyns-eks-keeper-kirvil-30-lever-ut-proffdrommen-i-italienske-sampdoria-na-retter-hun-kritikk-mot-norsk-rekruttering-av-unge-jentekeepere/411488|title=Lyns eks-keeper Kirvil (30) lever ut proffdrømmen i italienske Sampdoria|author=Høilund, Anders|work=[[Vårt Oslo]]|date=23 October 2022|language=no|access-date=3 August 2023}}</ref> She played 5 [[Serie A (women's football)|Serie A]] games for Sampdoria.<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|kirvil-odden-sundsfjord}}</ref> The club fell into economic disarray in 2023, allegedly with months of unpaid wages.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telen.no/kirvil-30-er-tilbake-fra-fotballkontrakten-i-italia-en-periode-gikk-vi-tre-maneder-uten-lonn/s/5-75-680085|title= Kirvil (30) er tilbake fra fotballkontrakten i Italia: – En periode gikk vi tre måneder uten lønn|author=Solheim, Iselin Moen|authorlink=Iselin Moen Solheim|date=12 July 2023|work=Telen|language=no|access-date=3 September 2023}}</ref> She returned to Lyn during the summer 2023 transfer window.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://lyndamer.no/nyheter/jeg-har-stor-tro-pa-laget-og-alt-som-skjer-i-klubben-om-dagen/|title=– Jeg har stor tro på laget og alt som skjer i klubben om dagen|author=Nordeng, Thomas|date=4 July 2023|publisher=Lyn|language=no|access-date=3 August 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Odden was born as Kirvil Schau Odden. In 2017 she married Charlotte Sundsfjord. The couple has one child. Alongside her football career, Odden has held a job as head of IT at Lysejordet Primary School.<ref name=telen20/>

'''Karl Hannes Sanh Furuhagen Hervieu''' (born 9 April 1989) is a Swedish politician of the [[Centre Party (Sweden)|Centre Party]]. Since 2025, he has served as the party secretary of the Centre Party.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Radio |first=Sveriges |date=2025-11-19 |title=Hannes Hervieu blir ny partisekreterare för C - Ekot |url=https://www.sverigesradio.se/artikel/karin-ernlund-slutar-som-c-partisekreterare |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=www.sverigesradio.se |language=sv}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Hervieu have been an active member of the Centre Party from his early teenage years. From 2013 to 2015, he served as chairman of [[:sv:Centerstudenter|Centerstudenter]].<ref name=":1">{{cite web |date=20 January 2015 |title=C-studenters ordförande till Fredrick Federley |url=https://dagensopinion.se/artikel/c-studenters-ordforande-till-fredrick-federley/ |work=Dagens Opinion |language=sv}}</ref> Parallel to his chairmanship of Centerstudenter, Hervieu began working as campaign manager for the campaign that brought [[Fredrick Federley]] into the [[European Parliament]] for the Centre Party in the [[2014 European Parliament election]]. <ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-01-20 |title=Hannes Hervieu ny pressansvarig hos Fredrick Federley (C) - Altinget |url=https://www.altinget.se/artikel/hannes-hervieu-ny-pressansvarig-hos-fredrick-federley-c |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=www.altinget.se}}</ref>

Hervieu ran for the [[Riksdag]] in the 2014 general election for the Centre Party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johansson |first=Peter |date=2014-04-04 |title=Centerpolitiker anklagar M: ”De kopierar våra förslag” |url=https://omni.se/centerpolitiker-anklagar-m-de-kopierar-vara-forslag/a/0e84cff1-4964-44ee-a484-b147cccfdef3 |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=Omni |language=sv}}</ref> He received 407 personal votes and was elected as a substitute member.

In January 2015, Hervieu began working as press officer and communications strategist for Fredrick Federley and the Centre Party in the European Parliament.<ref name=":1" /> In August 2016, he returned to Sweden from his position in [[Brussels]] and took up the role of press secretary to [[Annie Lööf]], the party leader for the Centre Party at the time. He held this position until 2019, when he moved to a job in the private sector.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-02-06 |title=Annie Lööf förlorar nära medarbetare |url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/kanbxL |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=www.aftonbladet.se |language=sv}}</ref>

From January to February 2021, he served as a member of the [[Riksdag]] covering for Johan Hedin.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riksdagen.se/sv/ledamoter-och-partier/ledamot/hannes-hervieu_95d25487-ff55-468d-a188-a6c6b4006377/|title=Hannes Hervieu (C)|publisher=[[Riksdag]]|language=sv}}</ref> 

In August 2025, Hervieu returned to the Centre Party and became chief of staff to the then party leader [[Anna-Karin Hatt]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hannes Hervieu rekryteras som stabschef till Anna-Karin Hatt {{!}} Centerpartiet |url=https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/3985036/hannes-hervieu-rekryteras-som-stabschef-till-anna-karin-hatt?publisherId=3237070&lang=sv |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=via.tt.se |language=sv}}</ref> In November 2025, Hervieu was appointed party secretary of the Centre Party, shortly after [[Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist]] was elected as the new party leader.<ref name=":0" />

=== Personal life ===
Hervieu is married and has two children.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-28 |title=Centertoppen Hannes Hervieu: ”Bara Vänsterpartiet vill ha Vänsterpartiet i regeringen” |url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/aJPOkE |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=www.aftonbladet.se |language=sv |trans-quote="Family: Wife and two children, aged 5 and 1,5."}}</ref>

'''Sho Kasamatsu''' (Japanese: 笠松 将, born November 4, 1992) is a Japanese actor.  
He is known for his performances in the television dramas ''[[Tokyo Vice (TV series)|Tokyo Vice]]'' (2022–2024), ''[[Gannibal (TV series)|Gannibal]]'' (2022–2023), and ''[[Love You as the World Ends]]'' (2021), as well as the films ''Flowers and Rain'' (2020) and ''[[Ring Wandering]]'' (2022).

== Early life ==
Kasamatsu was born in [[Nagoya]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], Japan. He was scouted by an agency in Nagoya while in his second year of high school.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://realsound.jp/movie/2019/05/post-362814_2.html|title=Sho Kasamatsu reveals his passion for acting: “I can't quit until I become number one”|work=Real Sound|date=May 18, 2019}}</ref> After graduation, he moved to Tokyo at age 18. Until around 20, he worked part-time in restaurants while applying for background roles in films.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://gendai.media/articles/-/92519?imp=0|title=Sho Kasamatsu: The actor who drew attention in the final episode of NHK's “Reach Beyond the Blue Sky”|work=FRaU|date=February 19, 2022}}</ref>

He began to take acting seriously after being inspired by other performers on set, later auditioning for small stage plays to gain experience.<ref name="switch2019.2">{{Cite journal|author=Tomohito Makino|title=NEWCOMER'S VOICE|journal=SWITCH|volume=37|issue=2|date=February 2019}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2017, Kasamatsu joined the Dongyu Club talent agency after leaving AAA (Triple A). By 2019, he had appeared in 18 television dramas and films in a single year, ranking first among male actors in their 20s for total number of roles.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO49775810T10C19A9000000/|title=Sho Kasamatsu tops 20s male actor rankings for number of roles|work=Nikkei Style|date=September 23, 2019}}</ref>

Kasamatsu played the rapper SEEDA in the 2020 film ''Flowers and Rain'', his first leading role in a feature film.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mikiki.tokyo.jp/articles/-/23738/|title=Sho Kasamatsu talks about “Flowers and Rain” and his passion for acting|work=Mikiki|date=December 11, 2019}}</ref>

In 2020, a contract dispute arose during his transfer from Dongyu Club to [[Horipro]] through Fine Entertainment, following his appearance in ''[[Love You as the World Ends]]'' (NTV). The disagreement was resolved later that year, and Kasamatsu officially joined Horipro.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dailyshincho.jp/article/2023/07121100/?all=1&page=2|title=Sho Kasamatsu moves to CAA after agency dispute|work=Daily Shincho|date=July 12, 2023}}</ref>

In June 2022, he signed with the U.S.-based management company [[Brookside Artist Management]] and talent agency [[Creative Artists Agency]] (CAA). In May 2023, Kasamatsu left Horipro to establish his own independent office.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.oricon.co.jp/news/2281197/full/|title= 笠松将、ホリプロ退所で個人事務所立ち上げ「言葉に出来ぬほどの感謝」|access-date= October 30, 2025|date= June 1, 2023|website= Oricon|language=ja}}</ref>

His international recognition grew with major roles in ''[[Tokyo Vice (TV series)|Tokyo Vice]]'' (2022) and ''[[Gannibal (TV series)|Gannibal]]'' (2022–2023), the latter distributed on [[Disney+]].

In 2025, Kasamatsu began his activities in South Korea. He appeared in the [[Netflix]] film ''[[Good News (2025 film)|Good News]]'' as Denji, the leader of a hijackers<ref>{{cite web|title='굿뉴스' 韓-日 톱 배우들의 앙상블 기대케하는 스틸 공개|trans-title=''Good News'' Unveils Stills Showcasing the Ensemble of Top Korean and Japanese Actors|url=https://enews.imbc.com/News/RetrieveNewsInfo/473832|work=iMBC|language=ko|author=Kim Kyung-hee|date=August 26, 2025|access-date=July 4, 2026}}</ref>, and in the [[Seoul Broadcasting System|SBS]] series ''[[Taxi Driver (South Korean TV series)|Taxi Driver]]'' Season 3 as Keita Matsuda, the head of the Japanese criminal syndicate Neko Money.<ref name="xportsnews_2081507" /> He is set to appear in the South Korean films ''Scandal'' and ''[[Shaving (2026 film)|Shaving]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=[단독] ‘대세’ 카사마츠 쇼, 차기작은 변요한·이솜과…‘파문’ 출연 확정|trans-title=[Exclusive] Rising Star Kasamatsu Sho Confirmed to Star in "Scandal" Alongside Byun Yo-han and Esom|url=https://isplus.com/article/view/isp202601070196|work=IS Plus|language=ko|author=Jang Ju-yeon|date=January 8, 2026|access-date=July 4, 2026}}</ref><ref name="sportschosun_042660002790" />

On June 28, 2026, Kasamatsu signed an exclusive management contract with the South Korean agency Star Platinum, marking the beginning of his full-scale activities in South Korea.<ref>{{cite web|title=카사마츠 쇼, 국내 매니지먼트 전속 계약…본격 韓활동 신호탄|trans-title=Kasamatsu Sho Signs Exclusive Korean Management Contract, Signaling the Start of Full-Scale Activities in Korea|url=https://sports.donga.com/ent/article/all/20260628/134193808/1|work=Sports DongA|language=ko|author=Lee Seung-mi|date=June 28, 2026|access-date=July 4, 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Kasamatsu has described himself as having "intense emotional swings, from high energy to irritation."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wanibookout.com/23364/|title=Sho Kasamatsu talks about playing a delinquent in 'Demekin'|work=WANIBOOKOUT|date=November 27, 2017}}</ref>  
His motto is "Life is a journey to find your motto."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cinematoday.jp/page/A0006403|title=Sho Kasamatsu transforms completely depending on his roles|work=Cinema Today|date=January 6, 2019}}</ref>

He trains three to four times a week and maintains a large appetite, recalling that he once ate up to seven meals a day as a student-athlete.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://i-voce.jp/feed/1284449/|title=Sho Kasamatsu trains at the gym 3–4 times a week even during film shoots|work=VoCE|date=February 4, 2022}}</ref>

'''Sidney Franklin Buehner''' (born {{Birth date|1990|1|15}})<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Sidney Franklin - In Biographical Summaries of Notable People |url=https://www.myheritage.com/research/record-10182-2919078/sidney-franklin-in-biographical-summaries-of-notable-people |access-date=2025-12-07 |website=[[MyHeritage]]}}</ref> is an American actor, [[tap dancer]], and film director who appeared in the series ''[[Watch Over Me]]'' (2006–2007), the film [[Excision (film)|''Excision'']] (2012), a production of [[Legally Blonde (musical)|''Legally Blonde'']] (2025), and multiple productions at [[La Jolla Playhouse]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2008-10-20 |title=Old Globe costumes stage a comeback at sale |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2008/10/20/old-globe-costumes-stage-a-comeback-at-sale/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251120212710/https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2008/10/20/old-globe-costumes-stage-a-comeback-at-sale/ |archive-date=2025-11-20 |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Bell |first=Diane |date=2000-06-27 |title=Local boy and Jacumba to star in quirky series |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/271674496 |access-date=2025-11-20 |work=[[San Diego Union Tribune]] |id={{ProQuest|271674496}} |via=[[Proquest]]}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Franklin was born on January 15, 1990 in [[San Diego, California]].<ref name=":1" /> In 2008, he lived in [[College Area, San Diego]].<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
In the late 2000s, Franklin starred in ''[[Watch Over Me]]''. In 2012, he was cast in [[Excision (film)|''Excision'']] and ''Stalked at 17'' by [[Lifetime (TV channel)|Lifetime]].<ref name=":4" /> In 2014, Franklin was a tap dance [[choreographer]] for San Diego Dance Theater<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Accomando |first=Beth |author-link=Beth Accomando |date=2014-08-21 |title='Sweat' — Hot Dances For The Hot Summer Nights |url=https://www.kpbs.org/news/arts-culture/2014/08/21/sweat-hot-dances-hot-summer-nights |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[KPBS Public Media]] |language=en}}</ref> and a member of Ballet 360.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eitland |first=Kris |date=2014-07-10 |title=San Diego Fringe: 'Dr. Frankenstein' a Freaky Hit with Heart |url=https://sandiegostory.com/san-diego-fringe-dr-frankenstein-freaky-hit-heart/ |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=San Diego Story}}</ref> He was part of the [[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike]] at [[San Diego Comic-Con]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Upadhayay |first=Prapti |date=2023-07-22 |title=SAG-AFTRA actors stand tall at San Diego Comic-Con, demand fair pay amidst AI threat |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/anime/sagaftra-actors-stand-tall-at-san-diego-comic-con-demand-fair-pay-amidst-ai-threat-101690025251846.html |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=[[Hindustan Times]] |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, he starred in a production of [[Legally Blonde (musical)|''Legally Blonde'']] and was cast in ''You Fired a Tech Genius'' by [[ReelShort]].<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" />
